title: Vice-President flags off Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally of MPs, commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram
subtitle:
Har Ghar Tiranga has become a People's Movement , It Gives Visible Form to the Spirit of Vande Mataram: Vice-President

Vande Mataram transformed love for the motherland into a national duty: Vice President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 11:03AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today flagged off the Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally with Members of Parliament and other public representatives at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, commemorating 150 years of the National Song, Vande Mataram.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan flagged off a special Bike Rally with Members of Parliament as part of
#HarGharTiranga
2026, organised by the Ministry of Culture, commemorating the 150th anniversary of our National Song, ‘Vande Mataram’.
Union Ministers Shri Kiren…
pic.twitter.com/MeN5LOCQRt
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
August 12, 2026
The rally proceeded from Bharat Mandapam to Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, carrying the message of national pride, unity and citizen participation.
Addressing the gathering, he said Vande Mataram transformed love for the motherland into a national duty and became a powerful expression of the spirit of India's freedom struggle. He recalled how its immortal words inspired countless freedom fighters with courage, sacrifice and hope.
Recalling his recent visit to the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, the Vice-President said his visit to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island and the historic Cellular Jail had been deeply moving. He recalled Netaji's hoisting of the Tricolour in 1943 and the sacrifices of freedom fighters imprisoned in Cellular Jail, many of whom went to the gallows with the cry of Vande Mataram.
Highlighting the nationwide impact of the National Song, Vande Mataram, in India’s freedom struggle, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled the contributions and sacrifices of freedom fighters and leaders from Tamil Nadu, including V. O. Chidambaram Pillai, Subramaniya Siva, Tiruppur Kumaran and Vanchinathan, as well as national poet Subramania Bharati, who carried the spirit and message of Vande Mataram to the people.
The Vice-President said the Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan, launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in 2022, has evolved into a people's movement, with citizens participating in Tiranga Yatras, bike and cycle rallies, cultural programmes and other activities. He said the Tricolour gives a visible form to the feeling of one Motherland and urged MPs and public representatives to promote the campaign in their constituencies and inspire citizens to hoist the National Flag with pride.
Union Ministers Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Shri Virendra Kumar, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Shri Kiren Rijiju and Shri Jitendra Singh along with Members of Parliament, and other public representatives, participated in the rally.

title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS SHRI KOVIND’S STORY AS AN ENDURING SOURCE OF “INSPIRATION FOR GENERATIONS”
subtitle:
PRIME MINISTER RELEASES AUTOBIOGRAPHY OF FORMER PRESIDENT SHRI RAM NATH KOVIND

SHRI KOVIND’S AUTOBIOGRAPHY PRESENTS AN EXTRAORDINARY JOURNEY OF STRUGGLE, RESOLVE, AND ACHIEVEMENT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

SHRI KOVIND UPHELD CONSTITUTIONAL TRADITIONS WITH UNWAVERING COMMITMENT TO SOCIAL HARMONY AND INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

DURING COVID-19 PANDEMIC, SHRI KOVIND INSTILLED COURAGE AND CONFIDENCE AMONG PEOPLE AND MADE RASHTRAPATI BHAVAN MORE ACCESSIBLE: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 9:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today released the autobiography of former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind, titled ‘Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles’ at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla was present on the occasion and described the release of the book as a matter of great pride and significance.
Speaking at the distinguished gathering, Shri Birla observed that the autobiography of former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind, an embodiment of high constitutional ideals, presents an extraordinary journey of determination, struggle, and achievement. Recalling the challenges of Shri Kovind’s early life, including the difficulties he faced in pursuing his education, he said that his journey from a humble and economically disadvantaged background to the highest constitutional office of the country reflects his extraordinary resolve and serves as an enduring source of inspiration for generations to come.
The Lok Sabha Speaker noted that Shri Kovind’s unwavering commitment to constitutional values enabled him to leave an indelible mark as an advocate. His tenure as a Member of Parliament, he said, was marked by dedication to the welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, social justice, and probity in public life.
Referring to Shri Kovind’s tenure as Governor, Shri Birla mentioned that he provided a new direction to transparency, quality, and technological innovation in higher education. As President of India, he upheld the constitutional traditions of Indian democracy and demonstrated an unwavering commitment to social harmony and inclusive development. Further, through his visits to several countries, he also contributed to strengthening India’s international diplomatic relations, he added.
Shri Birla also mentioned that during the challenging period of the COVID-19 pandemic, Shri Kovind instilled courage, unity, and confidence among the people of the country and made the Rashtrapati Bhavan more accessible to the public. He described this as one of Shri Kovind’s significant achievements.
The Lok Sabha Speaker added that even after demitting the office of President, Shri Kovind continues to contribute to the nation, the Constitution, and society through his vast experience, reflections on public life, and commitment to social justice. Shri Birla expressed confidence that ‘Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles’ would bring before readers important episodes from Shri Kovind’s life and inspire them to play a purposive role in public life. He concluded by extending his warm congratulations and best wishes to Shri Ram Nath Kovind on the publication of the book.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi releases Autobiography of Former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind
subtitle:
Today, we have the opportunity to release the autobiography of Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji; I am happy to be a part of this program: PM

His journey reflects a life dedicated to public service and the progress of our nation:PM

My prolonged acquaintance with Kovind Ji and his special affection and warmth towards me have been my greatest assets: PM

Mahatma Gandhi, Babasaheb Ambedkar, Jyotiba Phule, and Savitribai Phule dreamed of forging a new India, where the absolute poorest and the most disadvantaged could get the chance to reach the very top: PM

Individuals like Kovind Ji have not merely transformed their own lives through their diligence and competence, they have also played a pivotal role in bringing that centuries-old dream and vision to fruition: PM

Even after retiring as President; he is working on 'One Nation, One Election'; Its resolution can start a new chapter in Democracy: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today released the autobiography of former President of India, Shri Ram Nath Kovind, titled “Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles”, at Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister said “Today we have got the opportunity to release the autobiography of Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji, and I am happy that I have become a part of this program,” remarked Shri Modi.
Reflecting on his deep personal connection with the former President, the Prime Minister highlighted his profound respect for Kovind ji's guidance and affection over the years. “My prolonged acquaintance with Kovind Ji, the good fortune of knowing him closely, his guidance in his capacity as President, and, above all, his special affection and warmth towards me, these have been my greatest assets,” noted Shri Modi.
Praising the depth of the former President's character and capabilities, the Prime Minister asserted that the literary work will serve as an enduring testament to the nation's democratic values. “I can say with full confidence that the autobiography of Ram Nath Kovind ji will in itself become a heritage for the Indian democracy and Indian society,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Acknowledging the vastness of Kovind ji's lifelong contributions to the nation, the Prime Minister, refraining from providing excessive details, encouraged the audience to discover the narrative firsthand. “In a book release, there should only be a 'curtain raiser', and it is better only if you all get the full benefit of the book by reading it!” remarked Shri Modi.
Highlighting the educational value of the memoir for the younger demographic, the Prime Minister expressed his desire for future generations to draw inspiration from the former President's words. “The new generation of the country should also read his writing and his experiences, from which everyone will get to learn a lot,” asserted Shri Modi.
Analyzing the title of the book, “Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles”, the Prime Minister interpreted its dual significance regarding personal hardship and national democratic success. “The struggles of life are his personal, but the victory achieved as a result of those struggles belongs to the Republic of India and its democracy,” observed Shri Modi.
Contrasting common human tendencies with the former President's magnanimity, the Prime Minister pointed out that while many blame society for their hardships, Kovind ji's generous heart deeply rooted in Indian values views society as an equal partner in his success. “When the heart is generous and there are Indian values, a person does not waste time finding faults in society, but focuses on its positive side,” noted Shri Modi.
Recounting a deeply tragic childhood incident from the autobiography, the Prime Minister shared the heartbreaking story of Kovind ji's mother losing her life in a house fire while trying to save essential household items in Kanpur Dehat. “You can imagine such an accident at a young age and losing a mother like this, how painful this must have been!” remarked Shri Modi.
Highlighting the resilience forged through this tragedy, the Prime Minister explained how a neighboring mother stepped in to assist with Kovind ji's upbringing, an act that profoundly shaped his understanding of societal harmony. “From this, he understood the power of unity and harmony of society, and those difficulties made Kovind ji even stronger,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Emphasizing the crucial paternal role following the tragedy, the Prime Minister noted how Kovind ji's father admirably steered the family and instilled strong values in his children. “The way he handled his family and gave values to the children is why Kovind ji considers his father his hero,” observed Shri Modi.
Tracing Kovind ji's reliance on education to overcome his lack of resources, the Prime Minister highlighted his extraordinary ascent to the highest office in the land. “He worked hard and did not let the lack of resources become a weakness, reaching a position which people had not even imagined then,” asserted Shri Modi.
Praising the former President's enduring humility, the Prime Minister recalled a deeply emotional public moment when Kovind ji returned to his village of Paraunkh, bowing to the soil and touching the feet of his former teachers. “His conduct placed such a picture of India's values in front of the world on which every Indian can feel proud,” noted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on the historical socio-economic setbacks caused by centuries of slavery, the Prime Minister honored the relentless struggles and visionary dreams of historical figures like Mahatma Gandhi, Baba Saheb Ambedkar, and Jyotiba Phule. “How many such great personalities had dreamed of the reconstruction of an India where the poorest of the poor could get the opportunity to reach the top,” remarked Shri Modi.
Connecting these historical aspirations to modern achievements, the Prime Minister credited figures like Kovind ji for actively realizing the centuries-old vision of an egalitarian society through sheer hard work. “Personalities like Kovind ji with their hard work and ability did not just change their own life, they also played a role in realizing that dream of centuries,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Stressing the continuous need for dedicated youth to carry this mission forward, the Prime Minister called for a generation that remains undeterred by obstacles and maintains the courage to forge paths toward national self-reliance. “With this very change, the resolution of building an empowered India will be fulfilled, and the path to a self-reliant and Viksit Bharat will be paved,” asserted Shri Modi.
Positioning the autobiography as a crucial motivational tool, the Prime Minister suggested that the detailed account of Kovind ji's life will serve as a definitive guide for shaping this necessary youth power. “The inspiration needed for the creation of such youth power, this autobiography of Kovind ji can become an important source of that,” observed Shri Modi.
Detailing Kovind ji's political genesis, the Prime Minister noted how working alongside Morarji Desai channeled his inherent desire for national service into a dedicated career in politics. “The feeling of national service that was inside Kovind ji, he found a path for it by working with Morarji,” remarked Shri Modi.
Highlighting a consistent track record of service, the Prime Minister commended Kovind ji's unwavering dedication to duty across his various roles in Parliament, as Governor, and eventually as President. “He worked making service his goal, and his tenure in Parliament is a witness to this,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Pointing to Kovind ji's tireless post-presidential contributions, the Prime Minister praised his ongoing leadership on critical national issues like 'One Nation, One Election', which holds the potential to revolutionize the country's democratic framework. “I believe the people of the country can learn a lot from this dedication to duty and spirit of service of Kovind ji,” asserted Shri Modi.
Acknowledging the immense difficulty of authoring an autobiography while remaining highly active in public life, the Prime Minister expressed gratitude to Kovind ji for completing this vital societal contribution. “Kovind ji has done this work for all of us because there is so much in his life in which all the people coming from poor deprived sections can see the shadow of their own life,” noted Shri Modi.
Detailing the broader moral lessons encapsulated within the text, the Prime Minister emphasized how the former President's narrative illustrates the enduring power of maintaining purity and honesty during the toughest times. “Kovind ji has continuously given this inspiration to the society on how this purity gives us the strength for national service while fulfilling the responsibilities of different posts,” observed Shri Modi.
Concluding the address with a strong endorsement of the book's historical value, the Prime Minister expressed absolute certainty that the literary work will serve as an essential archive for both personal and national milestones. “I am confident Kovind ji's autobiography will safely preserve not only the important memories of his life but also of our democracy,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM's speech during release of former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 11:19AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Our former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji, Honorable Speaker of the Lok Sabha Om Birla ji, Mrs. Savita Kovind ji, all the senior dignitaries seated in the hall - I may not be able to mention everyone, but it gives me great joy that this feels like a family gathering.
Brothers and sisters,
Today we have the occasion of releasing Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji’s autobiography. I am happy that I too have had the fortune of being part of this program. I have had a long association with Kovind ji, the opportunity to know him closely, to receive his guidance as President, and along with all this, his special affection and warmth toward me - this has been a great treasure in my life. From what I have understood of his life, from what I have seen of his capabilities, I can say with full confidence that Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji’s autobiography will become a heritage for Indian democracy and Indian society. His life journey, his contribution to society and the nation - there is so much I could speak about, but at a book release only a “curtain raiser” should be given. You must read the book fully to gain its complete benefit.
Friends,
To know Kovind ji’s life journey in his own words, to read his writing, his experiences - this will give the new generation much to learn. I warmly congratulate Ram Nath Kovind ji for this autobiography.
Friends,
Kovind ji has given his book a very apt title - “Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles.” The meaning is that life and its struggles are personal, but the victories that came from those struggles belong to the Republic of India, to Indian democracy.
Friends,
We often see that human nature is such that people credit themselves for success, and blame society for difficulties. But when the heart is generous, when Indian values are present, then a person does not waste time finding faults in society. He focuses on the positive side, and considers society an equal partner in his success. Kovind ji’s autobiography and its title are examples of this. Look at his life - born in a very ordinary family in Kanpur Dehat. He has described, and written in his book, how one summer day a fire broke out in his house. His mother, forgetting her own safety, tried to save the household items. For a mother in a simple family, every item is a means of raising her children. In that effort, she was trapped in the fire and passed away. Imagine - at such a young age, to lose one’s mother in this way, how painful it must have been. I was fortunate that my mother lived beyond 100 years and blessed me. Even so, I still feel her absence.
Friends,
This painful incident could have broken anyone, but it made Kovind ji stronger. A neighbor mother helped in his upbringing. From this he understood the strength of social unity and harmony. After this incident, his father’s role became even greater. The way his father managed the family, gave values to the children - that is why Kovind ji considers his father his hero.
Friends,
Amidst these childhood struggles, Kovind ji made education the path to strengthen himself. He worked hard, did not let lack of resources become a weakness. And he reached a height that people could not even imagine then - he became the President of a vast country like India.
Friends,
Even after reaching such a high position, Kovind ji’s humble personality and simplicity remained intact. I remember, as Prime Minister when I went to meet him at Rashtrapati Bhavan, he would do things beyond protocol. He would come to the car door to see off the Prime Minister. I used to request him not to do this, but he never left his humility till the end. After becoming President, when he went to his village Paraunkh, he touched the feet of his teachers and paid respect. He bowed to the soil of the village and thanked the ordinary people. The whole country saw that emotional scene. His conduct presented to the world a picture of Indian values that every Indian is proud of.
Friends,
In centuries of slavery, our country lost much economically and socially. Our ancestors struggled for centuries. Mahatma Gandhi, Babasaheb Ambedkar, Jyotiba Phule, Savitribai Phule - so many great figures dreamed of a new India, where even the poorest and most deprived could reach the summit. Personalities like Kovind ji, through their labor and ability, not only changed their own lives, but played an important role in realizing that centuries‑old dream and vision. Our efforts in this direction continue. In the future, we need many youths like Kovind ji, who are not defeated by troubles, who do not despair before difficulties, but who have the courage to make every goal easier through hard work. This change will fulfill the resolve of building a strong India. From here will emerge the path to self‑reliant and developed India.
Friends,
For building such youth power, Kovind ji’s autobiography can be an important source of inspiration.
Friends,
In his autobiography, Kovind ji has also described in detail his experiences with Morarji Desai. The spirit of service to the nation that was within him, the learning and path he gained by working with Morarji bhai - Kovind ji made politics and social service his path. He remained dedicated to his duties. He made service his goal. His tenure in Parliament is witness to this. As Governor too, he set an example. As President, we saw the same dedication. Even after retiring from the highest post of President, he did not rest. He is still working on important subjects like One Nation, One Election. He is awakening the nation. This is a subject whose solution can begin a new chapter in Indian democracy. I believe the people of the country can learn much from Kovind ji’s dedication and spirit of service.
Friends,
Remaining active in social life, finding time for an autobiography is very difficult. Kovind ji has done this work for all of us, because his life contains so much in which people from poor and deprived backgrounds can see reflections of their own lives. How an ordinary family, even in difficult circumstances, does not compromise with purity and honesty of life. How those ideals later become the foundation of our lives. How the values of hard times give us light throughout life. How this purity gives us strength for national service. While fulfilling responsibilities in different positions, Kovind ji has continuously given this inspiration to society.
Friends,
I am confident that Kovind ji’s autobiography will preserve not only the memories of his life, but also important memories of our democracy. Once again, I extend my best wishes to him for his autobiography. And I especially urge the young generation - this is the age of reels, social media influencers pull you here and there. In this age of shortcuts, remember one thing. At railway stations it is written - some people jump across the tracks instead of using the bridge. There it is written: Shortcut will cut you short. Even if you want to go by shortcuts, I urge the youth - read autobiographies of whoever you admire. Autobiographies give you the chance to understand the events of history in a different way. They are close to history. That is why I want Kovind ji’s effort to benefit future generations, especially the youth. Many congratulations. Thank you very much.
DISCLAIMER -This is the approximate translation of Prime Minister's Speech. Original Speech was delivered in Hindi.

title: Prime Minister shares a Sanskrit Subhashitam, highlighting the power of winning hearts through vision, thoughts, words, and actions

content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam today, highlighting the power of winning hearts through vision, thoughts, words, and actions.
The Prime Minister wrote on X;

title: PRESS RELEASE ON 393rd REPORT OF THE DEPARTMENT-RELATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORT, TOURISM AND CULTURE
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 10:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture headed by Shri Sanjay Kumar Jha, M.P., Rajya Sabha, presented its 393rd Report on “From Manuscript to Mission: Preserving, Mapping and Sustaining India’s Cultural Heritage in the Age of Artificial Intelligence” on Wednesday, the 12th August, 2026.
The Report was adopted by the Committee on 11th August, 2026. The Key Recommendations/Observations made by the Committee in this Report are enclosed.
The full Report is available on the website of Rajya Sabha
https://sansad.in/rs -→Committees→Department
related RS→Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture-→ Report
THE THREE HUNDRED NINETY THIRD REPORT OF DEPARTMENT-REL koi ATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORT, TOURISM AND CULTURE
SUMMARY OF
RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Enlarge the digitisation standard into a complete capture standard, settled in consultation with scholars, scientists and custodians and in force before the contracts reach full scale: a multispectral recovery tier for damaged and overwritten folios; surface-relief imaging as the standard for palm leaf; a materials record for significant manuscripts; and a dating protocol anchored at Indian accelerator laboratories with margins stated on the record. (Paragraph 5.1.2)
2. Institute, with the national scientific departments, a research and challenge programme to read manuscripts that cannot be opened, beginning with a census of fused and fire-damaged holdings. (Paragraph 5.2.2)
3. Build the national reading workforce: the Akshar Mitra citizen platform with two independent checks on every page and permanent contributor credit; the university compact under which unedited manuscripts become dissertation editions recognised as research of the first rank; and published priority lists so that effort chases textual value. (Paragraph 5.3.2)
4. Release every publicly funded page and verified transcription as an open national library of training pages with an annual public benchmark, and employ federated learning so that restricted collections contribute without an image leaving custody. (Paragraph 5.4.2)
5. Publish the open index of persons, places and works of the corpus, the time-layered atlas of Indian knowledge built upon it, and the register of scribal hands. (Paragraph 5.5.2)
6. Extract the astronomical and weather observations of the corpus, with the national scientific agencies, as open national datasets for Indian science. (Paragraph 5.6.2)
7. Constitute the standing programme to reunite the scattered corpus: a common catalogue of dispersed and overseas holdings; exchange of images; virtual rebinding by computer matching of leaves and hands; and the identification of Indian manuscripts held overseas, the acquisition of digital copies of them and steps to bring back originals where return can be secured, with reunified treasures proposed for the Memory of the World register. (Paragraph 5.7.2)
8. Build, with the Ministry of Ayush, the concordance connecting manuscript formulations to the national terminologies and the statutory pharmacopoeia. (Paragraph 5.8.2)
9. Build the Repository's architecture of trust: the international image interoperability framework as the access standard; community access protocols under which every custodian chooses, item by item, what is shown; and an embedded credential in every machine-produced rendering, with the Ministry advocating its preservation with the major platforms. (Paragraph 5.9.2)
10. Serve the living inheritance: oral heritage recorded through Indian-language speech recognition, beginning with the fewest surviving bearers; fonts, keyboards and voices for every encoded script, freely downloadable and offered to the major operating systems; and the technique of the last masters recorded in three dimensions, with personal designation, lifetime grant and successor duties. (Paragraph 5.10.2)
11. Put the map to work: the cultural and manuscript layers on the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan and in district planning; knowledge tourism circuits designed from them; and the mapped artisan joined to commerce through the Open Network for Digital Commerce with authenticity credentials linked to the map. (Paragraph 5.11.2)
Establish the guardianship framework: the machine-graded register of manuscripts at risk with preservation kits and connected loggers for custodians; district salvage annexes wired into the national alerting infrastructure with cultural first-aid training; and a published preservation architecture of distributed copies and a deep archive on century-lasting media. (Paragraph 5.12.2)

title: Third Meeting of Hindi Advisory Committee of Ministry of Ayush Held in New Delhi
subtitle:
Hindi Plays an Important Role in Strengthening Good Governance and Taking Ayush to the People: Shri Prataprao Jadhav

Emphasis on Strengthening Use of Hindi and Public Outreach in Ministry of Ayush
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The third meeting of the Hindi Advisory Committee of the Ministry of Ayush was held today at Kartavya Bhawan-I, New Delhi, under the chairmanship of Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
The meeting was attended by Hon’ble Members of Parliament Shri Rahul Singh Lodhi and Shri Gyaneshwar Patil, along with Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, members of the Committee and senior officials of the Ministry and its subordinate institutions.
Addressing the meeting, Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that the Hindi Advisory Committee is not merely a formal body but an important platform for strengthening the use and promotion of Hindi in the Ministry and making it an effective medium for public welfare and communication.
Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that the country is moving forward with the vision of ‘Viksit Bharat @2047’. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has laid special emphasis on the preservation, promotion and wider use of Indian languages. Shri Jadhav noted that the Prime Minister’s consistent use of Hindi at national and international forums has enhanced the recognition and respect for Hindi globally.
Shri Jadhav said that he makes efforts to ensure that maximum official work in his office is undertaken in Hindi. He urged officers and employees not to view the use of Hindi merely as a formal or constitutional obligation, but to make it an effective instrument of good governance, transparency and public outreach and an integral part of their day-to-day work.
Highlighting the importance of Indian languages in the Ayush sector, Shri Jadhav said that Ayush represents India’s rich and ancient knowledge tradition. Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa and Homoeopathy are gaining increasing popularity not only in India but also across the world.
Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, highlighted the efforts being made by the Ministry to promote the use of Hindi in official work, correspondence, publications, website, social media and public relations activities. He also informed the Committee about initiatives to encourage officers and employees to use Hindi through training programmes, workshops and incentive schemes.
The Committee discussed the need to make Ayush-related knowledge, research, scientific literature, public welfare schemes and achievements of the Ministry widely available in Hindi and other Indian languages. The members also deliberated on making Ayush-related information more accessible through Indian languages and further strengthening its outreach among the general public.
The Ministry’s Hindi house journal ‘Apratim Ayush’ was also released during the meeting. Smt. Purnima Bose, Deputy Director, Department of Official Language, Ministry of Ayush, welcomed the participants, while Dr. Prakash Kumar, Assistant Director, Ministry of Ayush, conducted the proceedings.
The meeting was also attended by non-official members Markandey Rai, Thinles Dorje, Sunil Mehru, Ramya Krishna Kanaparthi and Hemchandra Vaidya.

title: “One Herb, One Standard” to Strengthen Quality and Credibility of Traditional Medicines: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav
subtitle:
PCIM&H and IPC Renew MoU to Advance ‘One Herb, One Standard’ Initiative

Inter-Ministerial Partnership to Strengthen Harmonised Scientific Standards for Medicinal Plants

Renewed Three-Year Framework Builds on 50 monographs Developed in First Phase

The MoU will Establish a Stronger, Coordinated Framework for Standardisation of Medicinal Plants: Shri Prataprao Jadhav
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), Ministry of Ayush, and the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, renewed their Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the implementation of the “One Herb, One Standard” initiative today.
The MoU was exchanged by Dr. Kousthubha Upadhyaya, Director I/c, PCIM&H, and Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, IPC, in the august presence of Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Ganpatrao Jadhav, and Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, at Kartavya Bhavan, New Delhi.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that India’s traditional systems of medicine—Ayurveda, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa, Unani and Homoeopathy—are an integral part of the country’s rich knowledge traditions and medicinal plant heritage. He emphasised that ensuring the quality, purity and standardisation of medicines and medicinal plants through scientifically developed standards is essential for strengthening the quality and credibility of traditional medicines.
Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted the significance of the “One Herb, One Standard” approach, which seeks to establish a common, clear, scientific and reliable standard for the same medicinal plant used across different systems of medicine. He said that harmonised standards would help address potential confusion among stakeholders and establish a stronger and coordinated framework for the standardisation of medicinal plants.
Shri Jadhav further said that the monographs developed under the collaboration would take into consideration Indian standards as well as international quality requirements. He noted that strengthening Indian standards in line with global benchmarks would enhance the quality and reliability of Indian medicinal plants and products and contribute to their wider international acceptance. He also highlighted that common and clear quality standards would contribute to Ease of Doing Business by making processes more streamlined, transparent and effective for manufacturers, exporters, testing laboratories, regulatory institutions and other stakeholders.
Union Minister Shri Jadhav congratulated the leadership, scientists and officials of PCIM&H and IPC for their continued efforts towards the initiative and expressed confidence that the renewed three-year MoU would give fresh momentum to the standardisation of medicinal plants. He said that the inter-ministerial cooperation demonstrates how coordinated efforts among Ministries and institutions can strengthen the standardisation of medicinal plants and traditional medicines. He added that the initiative would contribute to protecting India’s rich biodiversity and traditional medicine heritage, while strengthening India’s position as a trusted global standard-setter in medicinal plants, traditional medicines and their quality standards.
The renewed MoU will continue the inter-ministerial cooperation for a further period of three years, with the objective of developing uniform, reliable and scientifically robust quality standards for single drugs of plant origin used across Ayurveda, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa, Unani and Homoeopathy systems of medicine. Under the renewed partnership, the monographs will take into account Indian standards as well as international quality requirements, strengthening Indian standards in line with global benchmarks and enhancing the quality and credibility of Indian medicinal plants and products in international markets.
The cooperation builds upon the MoU initiated in 2022 to promote and facilitate the “One Herb, One Standard” concept, under which 50 monographs of medicinal plants were successfully developed during the first phase. The renewed partnership will further expand this framework by harmonising standards for the same medicinal plant across different traditional systems of medicine, thereby reducing ambiguity among stakeholders and establishing a stronger and more coordinated standardisation mechanism. By bringing together the scientific and standard-setting expertise of PCIM&H and IPC, the initiative will strengthen quality assurance, support ease of doing business and contribute to safeguarding India’s rich biodiversity and traditional medicinal heritage, while enhancing India’s position in global pharmaceutical standardisation.
The renewal of the MoU reaffirms the continued commitment of both institutions towards advancing scientific excellence, quality, reliability and global acceptance of India’s traditional systems of medicine through a harmonised approach to botanical standardisation. The partnership is expected to further strengthen India’s position as a trusted global standard-setter for medicinal plants, traditional medicines and their quality standards.

Annexure-I
.
The details of financial, technical and incubation support provided to space startups through Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) are enclosed at
Annexure-II.
Further, NSIL, in coordination with IN-SPACe, has been transferring various technologies developed at ISRO/ Department of Space.  As on date, NSIL has signed 118 Technology Transfer Agreements for transferring 83 technologies developed at ISRO/ Department of Space to Indian Industry.
This includes critical space technologies like Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) technology, Indian Mini Satellite-1 (IMS-1) Bus, ISRO Laser Gyro (ILG), Tri-band (S, X, Ka) Antenna Feed, Ceramic Servo Accelerometer (CSA), X band Mini-SAR and Low Temperature Co-Fired Ceramic (LTCC) Multi Chip Module technology.
NSIL has transferred many technologies to Indian start-ups in the space sector and have been providing hand holding for them to successfully assimilate the technology and to use it for commercial basis. In addition to that NSIL also facilitates various Indian industries / Govt. PSU for utilization of ISRO technical facilities for validation of the technology / product being developed by them.
The Government has undertaken several proactive measures following the liberalization of the space sector, in order to promote participation of startups in satellite manufacturing, launch services, downstream applications and space-based technologies
Announced the Indian Space Policy 2023, where the roles and responsibilities of all the contributors of Indian Space Eco systems defined.
Brought out the decadal vision and strategy for the Growth of the Indian Space sector and Economy
Introduction of a liberalized Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) policy for the space sector.
Implementation of a discounted pricing policy to enable Non-Government Entities (NGEs) to access ISRO facilities.
Establishment of a ₹1,000 crore Venture Capital (VC) Fund to support space start-ups.
Launch of the ₹500 crore Technology Adoption Fund (TAF) to accelerate the development, demonstration, and commercialization of indigenous space technologies.
Facilitation of access to ISRO infrastructure, technical expertise, and mentorship to support private sector growth.
Launch of skill development initiatives to address the evolving workforce requirements of the space sector.
Establishment of a Technical Centre to provide affordable testing, validation, and simulation facilities for space systems.
Enabling transfer of ISRO-developed technologies to industry for commercialization.
Providing opportunities to validate space technologies through the PSLV Orbital Experimental Module (POEM) platform.
Launch of the "Satellite Bus as a Service (SBaaS)" initiative to develop indigenous satellite platform capabilities and accelerate satellite development.
Encouraging state government to establish the manufacturing clusters as well as common testing facilities to boost manufacturing.
As on today there is no proposal or plan to establish or support additional space incubation centres, testing facilities or innovation hubs in Andhra Pradesh.
The Government has undertaken several measures following the liberalisation of the space sector. These measures encompass policy and regulatory reforms, infrastructure access, technology transfer, funding support, and capacity building through skill development to foster a vibrant private space ecosystem
Transfer of technology
IN-SPACe is facilitating the transfer of available ISRO technologies to industry while also identifying and consolidating the technology requirements of industry for future technology development and transfer. Till date 118 Technology Transfer Agreements have been executed through NSIL.
To facilitate technology transfer, NSIL is promoting greater participation of private enterprises through transparent technology transfer processes and industry-friendly policies. It is promoting private sector participation through industry partnerships, capacity building, and opportunities across satellite manufacturing, integration, testing, and downstream services.
Further, IN-SPACe is taking forward the planned transfer of Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) and Launch Vehicle Mark-3 (LVM3) technologies to enable greater private sector participation in launch vehicle manufacturing and operations
Investment in the space sector
The Government has also introduced various investment support schemes for space startups, including the IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme, the Technology Adoption Fund (TAF), and the ₹1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund.  As a result of these policy interventions and the growing participation of the private sector, cumulative investments in Indian space start-ups have reached approximately USD 618.5 million as on 31 March 2026, with the investment landscape progressively shifting from early-stage seed funding towards larger growth-stage investment rounds
International Collaboration and Global Market Access
IN-SPACe actively engages with foreign governments, space agencies, industry, and other stakeholders to promote and facilitate international collaborations for the Indian commercial space sector, including startups.  The key initiatives undertaken by IN-SPACe include:
Strengthening bilateral and multilateral partnerships with leading space-faring nations.
Facilitating the participation of Indian space industries in international exhibitions, business forums, delegation visits, B2B engagements, and industry roundtables to enhance global market access.
Representing the Indian commercial space sector in Government-to-Government (G2G) dialogues and fostering partnerships with emerging space economies to promote exports, technology collaborations, and integration into global space supply chains.
These initiatives have enabled collaboration opportunities for the Indian private space sector with stakeholders across more than 30 countries
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP (PPP) MODEL FOR EARTH OBSERVATION SATELLITE CONSTELLATIONS
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government, through the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe), has formulated a Public Private Partnership (PPP) framework for the development, deployment and operation of Earth Observation (EO) satellite constellations, with a view to enhancing the country's space-based observation capabilities, space economy and building an indigenous, self-reliant Earth Observation ecosystem in the country.
Under this framework, Non-Government Entities (NGEs) including private industry, start-ups and, where relevant, academic and research institutions are enabled to design, build, own and operate Earth Observation satellite constellations on an end-to-end basis. The envisaged roles include:
Satellite manufacturing
: Design, fabrication, integration and testing of EO satellites, including 5 ultra-high resolution optical satellites with 4 bands, 3 multispectral satellites with 8 bands, 2 hyperspectral optical satellites with 250 bands and 2 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites in X-band, by Indian industry.
Launch services
: Utilisation of Indian launch vehicles (private/ISRO), for placing the satellites in to orbit.
Data generation and ground infrastructure
: Establishment of ground stations, mission control and data reception/processing infrastructure by the private consortium.
Downstream applications
: Development of value-added products, analytics and decision-support tools for Government departments, strategic users and commercial customers.
Academic and R&D linkages
: Collaboration with academic and research institutions for capacity building and application development.
The following financial assistance, policy incentives and institutional mechanisms have been put in place by the Government to encourage private investment in Earth Observation and allied space missions:
Antariksh Venture Capital Fund of Rs. 1,000 crores, announced to catalyse private investment in the space sector.
Technology Adoption Fund (TAF) of Rs. 500 crores, providing financial support of up to 60% of project cost for start-ups/MSMEs and up to 40% for larger industries, subject to a cap of Rs. 25 crores per project, to enable commercialisation of early-stage space technologies, including EO-related technologies.
Seed Fund Scheme, providing grants of up to Rs. 1 crore to start-ups and NGEs, including for applications in agriculture, disaster management, urban planning and marine domain awareness.
Common Technical Facilities, with an outlay of Rs. 500 crores, along with support to State Governments for setting up Space Manufacturing Clusters.
Differential pricing policy for NGEs buying Indian satellite data to provide demand certainty for EO data and services.
Transfer of Technology (ToT) from ISRO to NGEs, including for satellite sub-systems and launch vehicle technologies.
Facilitation support, including Resident Experts placed by IN-SPACe to provide technical assistance to industry at no cost, and a Pre-Incubation Entrepreneurship Development Programme.
Institutional single-window mechanism: IN-SPACe functions as the nodal authorisation, promotion and facilitation body for all NGE space activities, including EO missions.
These measures are complemented by the Indian Space Policy-2023, which provide the overarching regulatory and ease-of-doing-business framework for private participation in the space sector.
IN-SPACe has approved and signed an agreement for the country's first indigenous, fully commercial Earth Observation constellation under the PPP model with a private consortium named Allied Orbits Private Limited. The details are as follows:
Allied Orbits Private Limited Consortium:
Led by PixxelSpace India, along with Dhruva Space, PierSight Space and Satsure Analytics India.
Scope
: Design, build, own and operate a 12-satellite constellation having panchromatic, multispectral, hyperspectral and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) capabilities, supported by indigenous ground infrastructure.
Estimated investment
: More than Rs. 1,200 crores, to be invested by the consortium.
Timeline
: The constellation is to be developed and operationalised by the year 2029.
Manufacturing and launch
: All satellites are to be manufactured domestically and launched on Indian launch vehicles, with mission control based in India.
The PPP-based Earth Observation constellations are expected to strengthen national capabilities in the following manner:
Disaster management
: Near-real-time, high-revisit daily imagery for early warning, damage assessment and post-disaster response coordination.
Agriculture
: Crop health monitoring, yield estimation, soil and water stress detection using multispectral and hyperspectral data, supporting schemes for farmer welfare and food security.
Climate monitoring
: Enhanced observation of climate impact monitoring like land-use/ land-cover change, glacial and coastal dynamics, and environmental parameters to support India's climate action and reporting commitments.
Urban planning
: Improved mapping of urban infrastructure, land records and planning inputs for smart city and infrastructure development initiatives.
Border surveillance
: SAR and ultra-high resolution optical capabilities providing all-weather, day-night surveillance to support strategic and security requirements, while reducing dependence on foreign satellite imagery.
Space economy
: These initiatives are expected to strengthen indigenous manufacturing, generate skilled employment, attract private and foreign investment, and contribute to the Government's goal of significantly expanding India's share of the global space economy.
Overall, the PPP framework for Earth Observation is aimed at building a self-reliant (Aatmanirbhar), data-sovereign EO ecosystem, with the private sector as the primary driver of manufacturing and downstream innovation, while the Government continues to act as an enabler, regulator, and anchor customer.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SPACE VISION 2047
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Key space-based applications undertaken during 2026 by ISRO/DoS are:
·
For Agriculture
: Satellite-based national level crop sown and harvest area mapping for 2 crop seasons; All-India mapping of Kharif rice, Wheat, Jute crops; national level crop yield estimation for rice and wheat crops,
technology support for State level mapping of crops for Maharashtra (Soybean, Cotton, Paddy) and Madhya Pradesh (Soybean, Wheat, Gram, Mustard, Paddy), Insurance unit level estimation of crop yield in 10 States to support Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY); Jute crop surveillance in the major jute-growing states of India, namely Assam, Bihar, Odisha, and West Bengal.
·
For Disaster Management
: Near-real-time monitoring and mapping of floods, landslides, cyclones, forest fires, Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), droughts, and other natural disasters using data from Earth Observation satellites. The outputs are uploaded to the BHUVAN and National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM) portals.
Satellite and numerical model-based search and rescue tool installed at Naval Operations Data Processing and Analysis Centre (NODPAC), Indian Navy, Kochi for their operations.
·
For Climate Monitoring
: Climate-related parameters, such as Chlorophyll-a concentration, sea surface wind currents, wind stress, and surface-level winds derived from the EOS-06 satellite mission (using Ocean Colour Monitor-3 and Scatterometer sensors); and Cloud products from INSAT-3DS are periodically updated and disseminated through the National Information System for Climate and Environment Studies (NICES) web portal. Satellite based Extreme Weather Nowcasting tool has been developed and deployed for assessment towards operational implementation in IMD/MoES.
·
For other developmental sectors
: Using Geospatial technology, Planning and monitoring of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) activities; Watershed Development Component-Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (WDC-PMKSY); Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana- Housing for All (Urban) (PMAY-HFA(U)); status of road network of the rural parts of India under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY); assets created under Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY), Green cover along the National Highways; Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI); etc. have been carried out.
The integration of satellite-based services with Central Ministries/Departments, State Governments and local authorities are strengthening through:
· The integration of Indian satellite data and indigenous space platforms in many of the National flagship programmes carried out by Central Ministries, State Governments and local authorities.
· Implementing the Forecasting Agricultural output using Space Agro-meteorological and Land based observation-2.0 (FASAL 2.0) project funded by MoA&FW, GeoCrest on the ISRO-Visualisation of Earth Observation Data and Archival System (VEDAS) portal for operational crop monitoring and yield assessment.
· Generating and providing crop yield estimates for various major crops.
· Supporting State Departments by providing technical inputs, geo-spatial solutions to assist in natural resources management, monitoring of developmental activities, planning of new activities.
· Providing near-real-time satellite-derived geospatial products to Central Ministries, State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs), District Administrations, and line departments under the Disaster Management Support (DMS) Programme.
· Carrying out training, capacity-building programmes for stakeholders to facilitate the adoption of space-based information for agricultural and natural   applications; disaster preparedness, response, damage assessment, and recovery planning.
· ISRO/DoS has signed more than 15 MoUs with Central Departments/Ministries and State Departments for implementation of technology in Crop mapping, Climatic & Disaster risk assessment, satellite data-based Weather Forecasting, Water Resources monitoring, mapping and monitoring of mining activities, etc.
·
Satellite Communication forms a part of
flagship government
programmes like BharatNet and Digital India to expand the communication reach
with enhanced capacity for good governance including Gram panchayats. The extended reach of BharatNet using space technology bridges the digital divide, improves administrative coordination, promotes more connected governance and thus supports evidence-based decision-making. In addition, it caters to the emerging applications like broadband services to home and enterprise users, ubiquitous secure services to government users, wide connectivity for strategic services,
DTH television, Very Small Aperture Terminal (VSAT) services, In-Flight and Maritime Connectivity (IFMC), societal applications (like tele-education, tele-medicine and disaster management).
To expand access to geospatial and Earth observation data for research, industry and public institutions a number of measures are implemented. These includes:
· Providing open and free access to Indian Earth Observation (EO) data, having coarser than 5m Ground Sampling Distance (GSD), to all users under the ambit of Indian Space Policy-2023. All the products derived from free data are also disseminated free of charges to all the users.
· EO data having GSD finer than 5m are provided free of charge to Government Users and at fair price to non-Government users.
· Enhancing the web-based interfaces, streamlining data regulations, and offering operational users near-real-time products. Space-based observations are distributed in real time for various applications through portals such as Meteorological and Oceanographic Satellite Data Archival Centre (MOSDAC) and VEDAS.
· Providing On-Demand Processing Platform to users to support their cloud-based processing requirements.
· To encourage and accelerate the use of space-based observations in various applications by research; industry and public institutions, ISRO/DoS organizes training programmes and workshops as part of capacity building.
The roadmap for scaling up the use of indigenous space technologies to support national development goals under Space Vision 2047 are in the following areas:
·
Earth Observation
Applications
: Future Earth Observation applications and infrastructure requirements are identified and presented in National Meet-2025, held on 22nd August 2025 at New Delhi. These infrastructure requirements are compiled in ‘Outcome Report of National Meet - 2025 Leveraging Space Technology & Applications for Viksit Bharat 2047’. The development of indigenous technologies to meet these requirements is taken up as R&D activities by respective ISRO/DoS Centres.
·
Satellite communication
: Indigenous space technologies are being developed to adopt new technological solutions such as Flexible payloads, Direct-to-Device (D2D), Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) using 5G/6G standards, NB-IoT over satellite for M2M communication, for enhancing digital applications. Multi-orbit compatible broadband terminals in higher frequency bands with beamforming capabilities are being indigenised. Development of ground station network infrastructure for optical and laser communication considering future HTS feeder link requirements and establishment of operational quantum key distribution (QKD) systems are under progress. Indigenous sovereign N-GSO constellations are being planned to provide broadband service.
·
Satellite Navigation
: NavIC-Navigation with Indian Constellation as the primary positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) service across transportation, logistics, aviation, maritime, railways, defence, agriculture, disaster management, and smart city applications. Receiver technologies will be developed for NavIC-based Precise Point Positioning (PPP) and Real-Time Kinematics (RTK). This will pave the way for adoption of NavIC in high-accuracy applications. Integration of NavIC into current and upcoming telecom technologies like 5G/6G is also planned. Indigenous development of NavIC-enabled GNSS Baseband ASICs (Application-Specific Integrated Circuits) is also a priority, promoting self-reliance in chipset manufacturing. Adoption into industry standards is a critical component for accelerating adoption in the market. This aspect will also be aggressively pursued. The main focus on expanding the NavIC constellation, enhancing signal diversity, accuracy and global coverage, promoting mass adoption through integration in consumer devices and critical infrastructure, supporting domestic chipsets and receiver manufacturing, and fostering a vibrant private-sector ecosystem for application development. There will also be steps for extending service for lunar PNT.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Presents Government’s Roadmap for a Self-Reliant and Globally Competitive Nuclear Energy Ecosystem in Lok Sabha
subtitle:
India Accelerates Indigenous Nuclear Energy Push with Focus on SMRs, Thorium and Private Sector Participation: Dr Jitendra Singh

Dr. Jitendra Singh Highlights 100 GWe Nuclear Energy Target by 2047, Indigenous SMRs and Three-Stage Nuclear Programme

Government Strengthens Nuclear Self-Reliance through SHANTI Act, Domestic Manufacturing and Advanced Reactor Technologies

At Least Five Indigenous Small Modular Reactors Targeted by 2033 as India Expands Next-Generation Nuclear Capabilities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 3:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India is steadily strengthening its indigenous nuclear energy ecosystem with a focus on advanced reactor technologies, Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), domestic manufacturing capabilities, private-sector participation and long-term utilisation of the country’s abundant thorium resources, Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions and Prime Minister’s Office, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s long-term nuclear energy strategy continues to be guided by the country’s three-stage nuclear power programme, aimed at sustainable utilisation of its vast thorium reserves for long-term energy security. The strategy has received further impetus through the Nuclear Energy Mission announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, with an objective of expanding nuclear energy capacity to 100 GWe by 2047.
The Government has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition. This includes deployment of large indigenous reactors such as 700 MWe Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) and advanced reactor designs at greenfield sites, alongside development and deployment of Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) at brownfield locations, including retiring fossil-fuel-based power plants, captive plants for energy-intensive industries and off-grid applications in remote areas.
A key objective under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous SMRs by 2033. The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), a constituent unit of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies, including the 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200) and 55 MWe SMR-55 for power generation. BARC is also developing a High Temperature Gas Cooled Reactor (HTGCR) of up to 5 MWth capacity, which can be coupled with a suitable thermochemical cycle for hydrogen production.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the continuing work of the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) in advancing the second stage of India’s nuclear power programme. IGCAR is pursuing multidisciplinary scientific research and advanced engineering development for Sodium Cooled Fast Breeder Reactors and associated closed fuel-cycle facilities, technologies that remain a cornerstone of India’s long-term nuclear strategy.
Emphasising the Government’s efforts to create a broader domestic nuclear ecosystem, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025 has been enacted to enable wider participation of both public and private entities in the nuclear sector.
The Department of Atomic Energy is encouraging Indian industry through knowledge-sharing and handholding for new SMR technologies, while simultaneously developing domestic nuclear vendors and strengthening the private-sector R&D ecosystem. Critical components such as low-alloy steel forgings for reactor pressure vessels and reactivity control drive mechanisms have already been realised through domestic industry, while development of other critical equipment has also been initiated with domestic industry and start-ups.
The reforms under the SHANTI Act envisage greater participation of private entities in nuclear manufacturing, engineering services, research and development and supply chains, while maintaining stringent standards of nuclear safety, security and safeguards. The Act also provides statutory status to the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, thereby reinforcing the framework for robust regulatory oversight.
On thorium, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India is pursuing its Three-Stage Nuclear Power Programme, based on a closed fuel cycle, to optimise utilisation of its uranium resources and progressively harness its abundant thorium reserves. Thorium, being a fertile material, needs to be converted into fissile uranium-233 in a nuclear reactor before it can be used for energy generation.
Under the first stage, natural uranium is used as fuel in PHWRs, followed by reprocessing of spent fuel to extract plutonium. In the second stage, Fast Breeder Reactors utilise plutonium to generate additional fissile material. The third stage envisages large-scale utilisation of thorium through uranium-233 bred from thorium, after adequate capacity of Fast Breeder Reactors has been established.
India has already undertaken sustained R&D towards thorium utilisation. Thorium Oxide (Thoria) pellets have been used in the initial cores of operating PHWRs, while Thoria-based fuels have also been irradiated in BARC research reactors. The irradiated Thoria pins have been reprocessed to obtain uranium-233, which has subsequently been fabricated as fuel for the KAMINI reactor at IGCAR, Kalpakkam.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Government is undertaking a range of measures to build a globally competitive, self-reliant and technologically advanced nuclear energy ecosystem. These include implementation of the Nuclear Energy Mission, development of indigenous SMRs, strengthening of domestic nuclear manufacturing and supply chains, continued capacity building in reactor design, manufacturing, construction and the nuclear fuel cycle, as well as expansion of indigenous nuclear medicine infrastructure through the Isotope Production Reactor (IPR) to augment domestic production of medical isotopes.
The Government’s approach, therefore, combines indigenous technology development, expansion of nuclear capacity, greater industry participation, advanced reactor research and sustained investment in the nuclear fuel cycle, with the larger objective of strengthening India’s energy security and technological self-reliance.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: THIRD-PARTY SECURITY AUDITS OF NUCLEAR POWER PLANTS
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 3:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Adequate measures are in place to ensure the security of nuclear power plants. Periodic security assessments are conducted both internally and by AERB, at all Nuclear Power Plant sites including Kudankulam. Additionally, assessments of nuclear power plants are also conducted by external Government agencies. The observations made are reviewed; monitored and necessary upgrades are carried out for compliance.
In all nuclear power plants, state of the art security measures are in place. Besides other provisions, Electronic Security and Surveillance systems like Perimeter Intrusion Detection System, Access Control System, X-Ray Baggage Inspection System, CCTV Monitoring System, etc are in place at all operating Nuclear Power Plants. These systems are implemented as an integral part of the Nuclear Power Plants. The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) also conducts regulatory inspection in respect of nuclear security of all Nuclear Power Plants.
Cybersecurity of nuclear installations is accorded the highest priority. Continuous monitoring and surveillance mechanisms are in place to detect and respond to cyber threats. Appropriate preventive and protective measures including access controls, regular security audits, vulnerability assessments, incident response mechanisms and capacity-building programmes are implemented. Further, CERT-in enhances the national cyber security posture by issuing alerts and advisory on emerging cyber threats and vulnerabilities, coordinating incident response and advisory remedial measures to affected organisations and operating the National Cyber Coordination Centre (NCCC).
Emergency Preparedness Plans (EPPs) approved by the regulatory authority are put in place at all Nuclear Power Plant sites including Kudankulam. Periodic exercises are also carried out involving various stakeholders including, local administration, security agencies and nuclear plant authorities. Feedback from the exercises is used to validate and improve the emergency preparedness plans. Presently, off-site emergency preparedness exercises viz. Table Top, Integrated Command, Control & Response (ICCR) & Mock Exercises are carried out once in two years, once in three years and as per NDMA schedule, respectively. The NPP authorities are regularly conducting the exercises at stipulated frequency. The ICCR exercise at Kudankulam NPP site was conducted on 15th April 2025. All the other NPP sites have also conducted their latest ICCR exercises since September, 2024 till date. For Kalpakkam site, the offsite emergency exercise has been conducted in ICCR (Integrated Command, Control & Response) mode on 17th July 2026 with the initiating event from PFBR and this exercise involves Participation of District Administration.
This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and
Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a
written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ENVIRONMENTAL SAFEGUARDS FOR HEAVY MINERAL SAND MINING AND RARE EARTH MINERALS
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 3:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research (AMD), a constituent unit of Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), has carried out exploration in the coastal tracts of Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu, for Beach Sand Minerals (BSM) and established a BSM deposit, viz. “Pudupuram-Cuddalore BSM deposit”, containing 1.912 Million tonnes (Mt) of Total Heavy Minerals (THM), including Monazite (0.005 Mt), Ilmenite (0.926 Mt) and Zircon (0.063 Mt).
The steps adopted by the Government of India to curb illegal beach sand mining & unauthorized export of strategic monazite sands in India are listed below:
Ministry of Mines (MoM) has issued Notification No. G.S.R 134(E) dated 20.02.2019 for amending the Threshold value of "Monazite" for BSM occurring in beach sand or placer deposits as "0.00%" in Total Heavy Minerals (THM), which resulted in bringing the overall BSM deposits of the Country under the complete control of the Government companies.
Directorate General of Foreign Trade, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India issued Notification No. 26/2015-2020 dated 21.08.2018 on export policy on BSM under which export of BSM have been brought under State Trading Enterprise and shall be canalized through IREL (India) Limited (IREL), a Public Sector Undertaking under DAE.
Monazite Test Certification (MTC) by AMD has been reintroduced for every export consignments of beach sand minerals as per the Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for Canalization.
Rule 45 of the Mineral Conservation and Development Rules, (MCDR) 2017 makes it mandatory for all miners, traders, stockiest, exporters and end-users of minerals to register and report on the production, trade and utilization of minerals to the State Government(s) and Indian Bureau of Mines or AMD as the case maybe. It facilitates end-to end national-scale accounting of all minerals produced in the country from pithead to its end-use, reducing the scope for illegal mining, royalty evasion, etc.
State Governments were requested to set up Task Forces at State and District Level to control illegal mining.
The MoM through Indian Bureau of Mines, has developed the mining Surveillance System (MSS), a satellite-based monitoring system which aims to establish a regime of responsive mineral administration, through public participation, by curbing instances of illegal mining activity through automatic remote sensing detection technology.
Section 23C of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 empowers the State Governments to make rules for preventing illegal mining, transportation and storage of minerals and for the purposes connected therewith. Hence, control of illegal mining comes under the legislative and administrative purview of the State Governments.
As regards, radiation hazard exposure to local fishing communities, adequate environmental safeguards are being taken in India during the planning phase of the projects pertaining to extraction of rare earth bearing minerals from the coastal area. Assessments to evaluate the potential environmental impact of mining rare earth bearing mineral, including effects on land, water, biodiversity, and local communities are conducted. In case of mining of minerals in coastal areas prior to execution of mining lease, a Letter of Intent (LOI) is issued to the Lessee with a condition that the lessee will have to conduct Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and submit the report to Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF & CC) including radiological survey of Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC). Only after clearance of MoEF & CC which tantamount that the impact is not detrimental, the lease is executed for mining.
Further, the mining operations for atomic minerals including RE bearing minerals from coastal areas are environment friendly as no drilling and blasting are undertaken unlike bulk minerals. The mined-out land is simultaneously backfilled, free of monazite on account of which background radiation in the deposits reduces to less than 0.5 micro-sievert per hour and subsequently original topography is restored followed by green belt development.
Health Physics Unit (HPU), an independent unit under Environmental Assessment Division (EAD) of BARC, Government of India monitors the radiological aspects in each of the plants of IREL.
This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a
written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: APPLICATION OF RADIATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SECURITY
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 3:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), a constituent unit of Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), has developed 72 improved varieties in different crops using radiation-induced mutagenesis along with cross breeding. These varieties have been released and notified for commercial cultivation across the country in collaboration with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and State Agricultural Universities (SAUs). These include 17 varieties in groundnut, 10 varieties in rice, 9 varieties each in mungbean and mustard, 8 varieties in urdbean, 5 varieties in pigeonpea, 3 varieties in sorghum, 2 varieties each in cowpea, wheat and soybean, one variety each in banana, sesame, linseed, sunflower and jute. Some of the desirable traits in these crops include higher yield, seed size, early maturity, climate resilient traits like drought, heat, salinity tolerance and resistance to diseases. Several of these varieties have high patronage from the farming community and are extensively grown in the country.
Genetic modifications induced through radiations in the different crops do not cause adverse effects. Prior to release, the developed varieties are thoroughly tested through multi-location evaluations over the years and released for commercial cultivation after attaining the superiority over the existing cultivars.
DAE has undertaken various initiatives to promote the adoption of improved crop varieties in the Indian farming communities. The steps include, large-scale quality seed production of Trombay varieties along with several state agricultural universities (SAUs) and supply to
State seed corporation,
ii. State agricultural departments,
National Institutes,
State agricultural Universities,
v. Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs),
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs),
vii. Farmer cooperatives,
Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs),
Seed companies and
x. Farmers in several States
In addition, DAE has participated in Kisan Melas, Field days, provided technical guidance and training on cultivation practices, conducted exhibitions in different states in collaboration with SAUs. DAE has also conducted Outreach programmes, field demonstrations, distributed seed minikits of the improved Trombay varieties and conducted Public Awareness Programmes on Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy to render benefit to hundreds of farmers.
DAE has developed radiation-based food preservation and food processing technologies to reduce the post harvesting losses and extend shelf life of agri products. Also, radiation-based protocols have also been developed for various agricultural products like vegetables, fruits, pulses, spices etc. The technology has been transferred to private entrepreneurs on non-exclusive basis, for commercialization and can be implemented through licensees.
Further, Government has implemented policy measures to expand the radiation technology for food preservation at the country level. Government of India has announced incentives for setting up of multiproduct food irradiation units under ‘Integrated Cold Chain & Value Addition Infrastructure’ of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) scheme across the Nation in 2024-25. This scheme is open for application by the interested stakeholders.
In the state of Uttar Pradesh, three food irradiation facilities have been commissioned till date in the private sector.
In agriculture, DAE has been consistently evaluating their developed breeding lines/mutants in different crops and their release in different agro-climatic zones in respective states in collaboration with State Agricultural Universities (SAU) and various ICAR institutes. DAE has research collaborations and Memorandum of Understandings (MoUs) with the State Agricultural Universities in Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and following ICAR institutes:
ICAR - Indian Institute of Groundnut Research, Junagadh
ICAR-National Soybean Research Institute, Indore
ICAR-Indian Institute of Rapeseed Mustard Research, Bharatpur
ICAR-Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Hyderabad
ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur and
ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana, Trichy.
Department also funds several research projects on mutation breeding and food preservation through Board of Research in Nuclear Sciences (BRNS) projects, an Advisory Body of DAE.
This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and
Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a
written reply in the Lok Sabha today.
