752 libraries have joined the ‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ app so far

Four libraries containing 2.80 lakh books have been linked with these rural libraries

The process of opening 63 libraries—each stocked with five to six thousand books—has begun across all villages in the Gandhinagar, Kalol, and Sanand assembly constituencies

Home Minister has personally prepared a list of books for libraries—books that will spark an interest in reading among children and inspire them to dive into the vast ocean of knowledge

Vans provided through the MPLADs will visit villages every fortnight to collect previously distributed books and deliver books registered on the app to village libraries
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today launched the 'Gramin Gyan Setu' app developed to integrate the libraries of Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency of Gujarat through video conferencing.
Addressing the event virtually, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah noted that today marks the birth anniversary of S.R. Ranganathan. He stated that the entire nation is celebrating the birth anniversary of Padma Shri Ranganathan as National Library Day, and that a new idea and concept—‘Gramin Gyan Setu’—has been launched in his Lok Sabha constituency. Shri Shah stated that the objective is to establish a library in every village—located centrally and near the school—to encourage children to engage with reading and learning. He noted that approximately 63 libraries have already been set up. Initiatives have been launched to open small libraries, each housing five to six thousand books, across all villages in the Gandhinagar, Kalol, and Sanand assembly constituencies. Union Home Minister mentioned that he personally curated a list of books for these multi-purpose, multi-dimensional libraries—books designed to spark an interest in reading among children and gradually inspire them to immerse themselves in the vast ocean of knowledge. Additionally, the libraries will stock books beneficial for the career development of adolescents and youth, as well as resources for state and national-level competitive examinations. Arrangements have also been made to ensure the availability of books covering the history of Gujarat, the history of the nation, the story of the freedom struggle, and the Revolution of 1857 right within the village.
Shri Amit Shah stated that cultivating a reading habit in children is not possible without encouragement from parents; however, for children who are motivated to study, four libraries—collectively housing 2.80 lakh books that will benefit them in the future—have been linked to these rural libraries. Union Home Minister mentioned that he has facilitated this service by arranging vans using his MP Local Area Development (MPLAD) funds. These vans will visit the villages every fortnight to collect previously issued books and deliver books registered on the app to the village libraries. He noted that children who are accustomed to visiting libraries containing 6,000 to 7,000 books will now have access to a collection of 2.80 lakh books.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated that while he had originally proposed the idea, Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel and the Gujarat government have integrated it with a new scientific approach. He noted that 752 libraries are now connected to the ‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ app. He emphasized that without study, it is impossible to gain even basic knowledge, let alone achieve mastery in any subject. He added that as individuals transition from childhood to adolescence, then to youth, and finally to adulthood, guidance from competent librarians regarding studies and their various dimensions can enable libraries to play a pivotal role in shaping citizens who are valuable to the nation.
Shri Amit Shah stated that the Mahatma Gandhi Library in Mansa has been linked to this library-related scheme. He mentioned that at the Mahatma Gandhi Library, he acquired basic knowledge across various subjects and gained in-depth understanding of some over a period of 16 years. After moving from Mansa to Ahmedabad, he became associated with the Gujarat Vidyapith library. He noted that Kakasaheb Kalelkar had created the Gujarat Vidyapith library as a means for many young people—like himself—to dive into the ocean of knowledge. The urge to gather information on every subject evolved into a habit, which subsequently transformed into a practice of study. He remarked that it was this practice of study that enabled him to contribute to a specific field, and the library played a pivotal role in this process.
Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated that these libraries and books have now been made available to the youth through the ‘hub-and-spoke’ model. While such facilities did not exist in his time, this program is now scientifically accessible to the current generation. He expressed his aim to have various institutions—such as Sastu Sahitya Mandal, Gita Press, the Bhupen Hazarika Institute, and the Thiruvalluvar Institute—connect online with libraries in Gujarat’s Gandhinagar district and at the state level. He expressed confidence that this facility would become available to students and readers through the use of technology.
Shri Amit Shah urged housewives across the country and the state to make productive use of their spare time by acquiring knowledge on various subjects and encouraging their children to study.

title: PREPARATORY ACTIVITIES FOR CENSUS 2027
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
First phase of the Census 2027 i.e., Houselisting and Housing Census has already been completed in 31 States/UTs. In the remaining states first phase of the census is scheduled to be completed by September, 2026. Further, as per the notification dated 3rd August, 2026 in the Gazette of India, second phase of the Census i.e. Population Enumeration in the UT of Ladakh and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the UT of Jammu & Kashmir and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the States of Himachal Pradesh and Uttrakhand shall be undertaken from 1st September, 2026 to 30th September, 2026 with a revisional round from 1st  October, 2026 to 5th  October, 2026. There shall also be an option for self-enumeration from 17thAugust, 2026 to 31st August, 2026.
Mobile applications for data collection and other digital platforms, including the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS) Portal, have been deployed for the conduct of the first phase of Census 2027. The facility of self-enumeration to the respondents through an online web portal has also been given for the first time in Census. Digital tools for the second phase of the census have been developed.
Training of Master Trainers, Field Trainers, Enumerators, Supervisors etc. for the first phase of Census 2027 has been completed/ in progress, in accordance with the notified schedule, in coordination with the States/ UTs Government.
Till now, a total amount of ₹4102 crore have already been released to States/UTs for training of Census functionaries, manpower assistance, technical infrastructure, payment of honorarium to Census functionaries etc.
This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha

title: DRUG TRAFFICKING CASES
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government of India has adopted a multi-pronged approach to curb cross-border smuggling including drugs, some of which are as under: -
(i)       Deployment of advanced surveillance equipment such as CCTV, drones, automatic number plate recognition systems, Pan, Tilt & Zoom (PTZ) Camera, Night Vision Device (NVD).
(ii)      Development of fencing, border outposts, roads, and helipads to enhance vigilance and mobility of security forces.
(iii)     Intensified area domination through patrolling, Naka points, and mobile teams to monitor illegal activities.
(iv)     Close collaboration between intelligence agencies and other organizations for real-time information sharing through established platforms.
(v)      Identification and management of designated entry/exit points to ensure controlled movement of people and goods.
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) was launched on 15th August 2020 by Department of Social Justice & Empowerment in 272 identified most vulnerable Districts. It has been extended to all districts of the country since August 2023. Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan intends to reach out to the masses and spread awareness about substance use with focus on higher educational Institutions, university campuses & schools. With the constant support of all the States, NMBA has been able to reach and sensitize more than 29.05 Crore people, including more than 11.05 Crore youth and 7.81 Crore women, through extensive awareness and outreach activities conducted across the country. 1.17 lakh + Nasha Mukti Mitr have joined the campaign.
To strengthen Centre-State framework to dismantle drug-trafficking networks Government has taken various measures, some of which are as under: -
(i)     To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) has been released on 26.06.2026. The Vision Document is to be implemented by the concerned Central Ministries/ Departments/ Agencies and the State Governments/UTs as per the action points and timelines specifically mentioned for each Central Ministry/ Department/ Agency. The four key focus areas outlined in the vision document are as under: -
Enforcement (Intelligence & Operations)
Precursors & Synthetic Drugs Control
Demand & Harm Reduction
Capacity Building & Coordination
(ii)    Established a 4-tier (Apex and Executive Committee at Central level and State and District level Committee at the State level) Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism for ensuring better coordination between Central & State Drug Law Enforcement Agencies and other stakeholders in the field of controlling drug trafficking and drug abuse in India. State-level NCORD meetings are chaired by the Chief Secretary while District-level NCORD meetings are held under the chairmanship of the District Magistrate to review enforcement, intelligence sharing and preventive measures.
(iii)   The NCORD Portal, developed by Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), serves as a comprehensive gateway and Knowledge Management System for all stakeholders from district to central levels.
(iv)   Joint Coordination Committee (JCC) meetings are held regularly in which all relevant Central and State agencies participate, to discuss investigation of important narcotics cases in the State. So far 11 JCC meetings at Central level and 75 JCC at the State level have been conducted.
(v)    A dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) headed by Additional Director General/ Inspector General level Police Officer is established in each State/UT to function as the NCORD Secretariat for the State/UT and follow-up on compliance of decisions taken in NCORD meetings at different levels.
(vi)  NCB, has shared a list of habitual narcotics offenders operating across the country with the State Police. The list was circulated to facilitate identification and initiation of suitable preventive action, including consideration of detention under the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PITNDPS) Act, 1988, against repeat and high-risk drug traffickers. The Drug Law Enforcement Agency (DLEAs) have effectively utilized the provisions of the PITNDPS Act and invoked detention orders against 810 habitual drug offenders all over the county during 2025 and 427 till June, 2026.
As per latest data published by National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) pertaining to the year 2024; State-wise/ UT-wise and drug-wise seizure under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985 during 2022-2024 is at Annexure-I.

title: AI-ENABLED CYBER CRIME PREVENTION AND DIGITAL IDENTITY PROTECTION
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. Accordingly, the States and Union Territories (UTs) are primarily responsible for the prevention, detection, investigation,  and   prosecution  of  cybercrime.   The Central  Government, through the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), supplements the efforts of States and UTs by providing policy guidance, technological support, capacity-building assistance, and financial resources to strengthen cybercrime management and enforcement capabilities.
To strengthen the mechanism to deal with cyber crimes including AI-enabled cyber crimes in a comprehensive and coordinated manner and to strengthen cyber resilience, the Central Government has taken steps which, inter-alia, include the following:
The Ministry of Home Affairs has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre’ (I4C)
as an attached office to deal with all types of cyber crimes in the country, in a coordinated and comprehensive manner.
The ‘National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal’ (NCRP) (https://cybercrime.gov.in) has been launched, as a part of the I4C, to enable public to report incidents pertaining to all types of cyber crimes, with special focus on cyber crimes against women and children.
The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ (CFCFRMS), under I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the fraudsters. As per CFCFRMS operated by I4C, till 30.06.2026, financial amount of more than Rs. 11,158 Crore has been saved in more than 32.80 lakh complaints.  A toll-free Helpline number ‘1930’ has been operationalized to get assistance in lodging online cyber complaints.
The Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC) platform, namely ‘CyTrain’ portal has been developed under I4C, for capacity building of police officers/judicial officers through online course on critical aspects of cyber crime investigation, forensics, prosecution etc. Till 30.06.2026, more than 1,63,344 police officers/judicial officers from States/UTs are registered and more than 1,61,957 Certificates issued through the portal.
Cyber Commando programme was launched by the Hon'ble Home Minister to establish a Special Wing of Cyber Commandos equipped with specialized training to counter cybersecurity threats in the country. The programme envisions the creation of a dedicated, skilled workforce capable of securing critical information infrastructure and supporting national cybersecurity efforts. 281 cyber commandos successfully completed training.
I4C, MHA is regularly organising ‘State Connect’, ‘Thana Connect’
‘
Bank Connect’ and Peer learning session to share best practices, enhance capacity building, etc.
A State of the Art, Cyber Fraud Mitigation Centre (CFMC) has been established at I4C where representatives of major banks, Financial Intermediaries, Payment Aggregators, Telecom Service Providers, IT Intermediaries and representatives of States/UTs Law Enforcement Agency are working together for immediate action and seamless cooperation to tackle cybercrime.
Seven Joint Cyber Coordination Teams (JCCTs) have been constituted for Mewat, Jamtara, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad, Chandigarh, Vishakhapatnam, and Guwahati under I4C covering the whole country based upon cyber crime hotspots/ areas having multi jurisdictional issues by onboarding States/UTs to enhance the coordination framework among the Law Enforcement Agencies of the States/UTs.
A Suspect Registry of identifiers of cyber criminals has been launched by I4C in collaboration with Banks/Financial Institutions. Till 30.06.2026, more than 30.48 lakh suspect identifier data received from Banks and 32.08 lakh Layer 1 mule accounts have been shared with the participating entities of Suspect Registry and declined transactions worth Rs. 25,698 crores.
Samanvaya Platform has been made operational to serve as an Management Information System (MIS) platform, data repository and a coordination platform for LEAs for cybercrime data sharing and analytics. It provides analytics based interstate linkages of crimes and criminals, involved in cybercrime complaints in various States/UTs. The module ‘Pratibimb’ maps locations of criminals and crime infrastructure on a map to give visibility to jurisdictional officers. The module also facilitates seeking and receiving of techno-legal assistance by Law Enforcement  Agencies from I4C and other SMEs. It has lead to arrest of more than 29,837 accused and more than 2,33,593 Cyber Investigation assistance request.
‘Sahyog’ Portal has been launched to expedite the process of sending notices to IT intermediaries by the Appropriate Government or its agency under clause (b) of sub-section (3) of section 79 of the IT Act, 2000 to facilitate the removal or disabling of access to any information, data or communication link being used to commit an unlawful act.
The Ministry of Home Affairs has established CyMAC (Cyber Multi Agency Centre) under the MAC (Multi Agency Centre) platform on 22.01.2025  with  the  objective  to  effectively  address  cybersecurity
threats, cyber espionage, misuse of emerging technologies and similar concerns against national security.
CERT-In issues alerts and advisories regarding latest cyber threats/vulnerabilities including malicious attacks using Artificial Intelligence and countermeasures to protect computers, networks and data on an ongoing basis.
National Cyber Coordination Centre (NCCC) implemented by CERT-In, examines the cyberspace to detect cyber security threats. It shares the information with concerned State Governments, organisations across sectors, and stakeholder agencies for taking action.
AI driven situational awareness systems are deployed by CERT-In to detect malicious domains and phishing activities for necessary mitigation.
CERT-In operates an automated cyber threat exchange platform for proactively collecting, analysing and sharing tailored alerts with State Governments and organisations across sectors for proactive threat mitigation actions by them.
Cyber Swachhta Kendra (CSK) is a service provided by CERT-In, which extends the vision of Swachh Bharat to the cyber space. Cyber Swachhta  Kendra  helps  to detect malicious programs and vulnerable
services and provide remedial measures to organisations across States and sectors.
CERT-In has empanelled 237 security auditing organizations to support and audit implementation of information security best practices.
Cyber security mock drills are conducted regularly to enable assessment of cyber security posture and preparedness of organisations in Government (Central & States) and critical sectors. Workshops along with these drills are conducted in States for facilitating coordination and information sharing in the area of cyber security.
To spread awareness on cyber crime, the Central Government has taken steps which, inter-alia, include; caller tune campaign, dissemination of messages through SMS, I4C social media account i.e. X (formerly Twitter) (@CyberDost), Facebook(CyberDostI4C), Instagram (CyberDostI4C), Telegram(cyberdosti4c), SMS campaign, TV campaign, Radio campaign, School Campaign, advertisement in cinema halls, celebrity endorsement, IPL campaign, engaged MyGov for publicity in multiple mediums, organizing Cyber Safety and Security Awareness weeks in association with States/UTs, digital displays on metro stations, railway stations and airports across, etc.
This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri
Bandi Sanjay Kumar
in a written reply to a question in the the Rajya Sabha.

title: NDMA'S NATIONAL PREPAREDNESS FRAMEWORK FOR BIOLOGICAL BIOSECURITY THREATS
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government is prepared to respond to any biological attacks in the country.
The National Disaster Management Guidelines on Management of Biological    Disasters,    2008    contain   a    threat-perception    and    risk-management framework covering biological safety, biosecurity and public-health preparedness. Biological and Public Health Emergencies have also been incorporated in the National Disaster Management Plan, 2019.
Continuous technical assessment, disease surveillance and early warning are undertaken by the concerned scientific, public-health and security agencies, including the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, National Centre for Disease Control, Indian Council of Medical Research and other designated agencies.
The NDMA Guidelines and the National Disaster Management Plan provide an overarching national framework for prevention, preparedness, early detection, containment and coordinated response to biological emergencies.
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) which  has been designated as nodal Ministry for biological disaster, has informed that health is a State subject and it provides requisite technical and financial support to States/UTs for strengthening their public health preparedness and response capacities against outbreak of epidemic prone communicable diseases. To enhance disease surveillance activities, MoHFW has strengthened the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) across the country, which allows for a decentralized system of response through trained multi-disciplinary Rapid Response Team (RRTs) to institute requisite public health control and containment measures.
In terms of laboratory strengthening, under IDSP, States have strengthened laboratories at district and State levels. Further, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has established a network of more than 150 Viral Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDLs) for strengthening of nation-wide network of laboratories for timely laboratory based diagnosis of pathogens. ICMR has developed two mobile Biosafety Level 3 (BSL-3) laboratories to provide essential on-site diagnostic services during outbreaks, especially in remote areas.
Funding support has been provided to States/UTs for health system strengthening to meet any exigency due to public health emergencies like pandemics, including strengthening of health infrastructure for enhancement of bed capacities, including ICU beds, expansion of laboratory network, surveillance, procurement of medical logistics etc.
With the long-term goal to better prepare our country against public health emergencies, Pradhan Mantri - Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM- ABHIM) has been launched with the intent to enhance the capacity of primary, secondary and tertiary health care facilities/systems and institutes for identifying and managing any new and emerging diseases.
Further, the Battalions of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) are trained in  basic Chemical Biological Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) course and the earmarked teams are equipped with requisite rescue, detection, monitoring and decontamination equipment.
NDRF teams are deployed on requisition from concerned State/District authorities across India.
NDRF conducts regular multi-agency mock drills on biological and biosecurity emergencies based on vulnerability profile of States/UTs. These drill involve all major disaster management stakeholder, including Civil Defense, SDRFs, Health Departments, Fire Services, Police, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs), district administration and hospitals. The exercises help test emergency response plans, improve coordination among agencies, enhance community awareness and strengthen overall preparedness. The response is carried out in accordance with Standard Operating Procedure (SOPs), the Incident Response System (IRS) and established inter-agency coordination mechanisms.
In addition, MoHFW also conducts series of mock drills for testing and strengthening cross sector response across India.
This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha.

title: Government Endeavours to Strengthen Credible Information Dissemination through PIB Fact-Checking, Public Service Broadcasting and Digital Media Regulations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 3:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Press Information Bureau (PIB), as the principal information dissemination agency of the Government of India, facilitates timely, credible and accurate communication in different forms through various media platforms. Prasar Bharati plays a key role in fulfilling the mandate of public service broadcasting. Information is disseminated in multiple languages, including regional languages and dialects, using various platforms.
The Government has established a Fact Check Unit (FCU) in PIB to mitigate fake news related to its programmes and policies. FCU verifies claims relating to Government Ministries, Departments, PSUs and other Central Government organisations through a structured fact-checking process. It disseminates verified information through various platforms.
Doordarshan and Akashvani further disseminate verified information through their news bulletins, programmes and digital platforms. DD News follows a multi-layered editorial mechanism involving rigorous fact-checking, cross-verification through multiple credible sources and editorial scrutiny before broadcast. PIB Fact Check content is regularly integrated into Doordarshan and Akashvani news and digital platforms to counter misinformation and false narratives.
The Government notified the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 under the Information Technology Act, 2000. The Rules prescribe due diligence obligations for intermediaries, provide a Code of Ethics for publishers of digital news and OTT platforms. It establishes a three-tier grievance redressal mechanism comprising self-regulation by publishers, self-regulating bodies and an oversight mechanism by the Central Government.
The Government promotes the film and media sector through initiatives including the Development, Communication and Dissemination of Filmic Content (DCDFC) Scheme, India Cine Hub (ICH) and the National Film Heritage Mission (NFHM). The DCDFC Scheme provides financial assistance for film festivals, promotion of Indian cinema, international participation, preservation and related activities. India Cine Hub facilitates film shooting permissions through a single-window mechanism and promotes India as a filming destination. NFHM undertakes preservation, restoration, digitisation and archiving of India’s cinematic heritage.
The Government promotes international media cooperation by strengthening its global engagement in media and broadcasting.
The Government organised the inaugural World Audio Visual & Entertainment Summit (WAVES 2025) in Mumbai in May 2025. It brought together the Media and Entertainment sector under the vision of making India a global hub for content creation through the “Create in India, Create for the World” initiative. The Summit provided a platform for Indian creators, producers and startups to engage with global buyers, investors, OTT platforms and technology leaders from over 100 countries.
In the broadcasting sector, Prasar Bharati maintains active engagement with broadcasting organisations across the world through content-sharing arrangements with international broadcasters and broadcasting agreements with partner organisations. It also has 48 active Memoranda of Understanding with broadcasters from different countries for cooperation in broadcasting, facilitating the exchange of content, professional expertise and best practices.
The information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to a Question asked by Dr. Alok Kumar Suman in Lok Sabha today.

title: National AI Skilling Initiative Records 60,253 Enrolments in Phase I; IICT and Private Sector Partners have Jointly Developed Curriculum to Equip Students with Industry-Relevant AI Skills
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The total number of applications received, and participants enrolled under Phase I of the National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Skilling Initiative as on date is 60,253.
The total number of participants who have completed 2 Modules of Phase I of the programme are 4620 and those who have completed all 4 Modules of Phase I of the programme are 552.
Phase I of the programme comprises four modules with a total duration of 33 hours, delivered through two learning platforms. The details of the Modules of Phase I are as under: -
Platform 1:
Module 1: AI Essentials – gain practical skills to boost daily productivity, synthesize data, and create content.
Module 2: Prompting Essentials – framework to write professional prompts.
Platform 2:
Module 3: Introduction to Generative AI – grasp Large Language Model (LLM) fundamentals and responsible AI guidelines.
Module 4: Generative AI Leader – master workflow automation and strategic Gen AI organisational transformation.
The details of Phase II, including the curriculum, modules and course duration, are under finalisation.
The curriculum has been jointly designed and developed by the IICT and private sector partners to impart foundational and practical AI skills. The advanced skilling component is conducted by IICT for joint certification.
The Government’s role has been to provide strategic direction and facilitating the implementation of the programme through IICT with the objective of enhancing AI literacy and equipping students with industry-relevant digital skills.
The information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to a Question asked by Adv Gowaal Kagada Padavi in Lok Sabha today.

title: RLB GRANTS RECOMMENDED BY SIXTEENTH FINANCE COMMISSION
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Sixteenth Finance Commission (FC-16), for the award period 2026-31, has recommended total grants amounting to Rs. 4,35,236 Crore for duly constituted Panchayati Raj Institutions/Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) in all 28 States including Chhattisgarh. Out of this amount, Rs. 11,664 Crore has been recommended for the State of Chhattisgarh.
The Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure vide letter dated 21.05.2026, has issued the Operational Guidelines for implementation of the Rural Local Body Grants recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission (FC-16). The FC-16 grants comprise two components, namely, Basic Grant and Performance Grant, in the ratio of 80:20. The Basic Grant is further divided into Tied and Untied Grants. 50 per cent of the Basic Grant is earmarked as Tied Grant, while the remaining 50 per cent of the Basic Grant and the entire Performance Grant are Untied. The Tied Grants are directed towards ‘Sanitation and Solid Waste Management’ and/or ‘Water Management’. The Untied Grants can be utilised by Rural Local Bodies for location-specific felt needs under the twenty-nine subjects enshrined in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution.
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has undertaken the following measures
to enhance Panchayats' Own Source Revenue (OSR) mobilization
:-
(i) The Ministry of Panchayati Raj, in collaboration with IIM Ahmedabad, has developed a training module on Own Source Revenue (OSR) to strengthen the financial self-reliance of Gram Panchayats. The module helps elected representatives and Panchayat functionaries understand how OSR is generated through tax and non-tax sources. As on 10.07.2026, u
nder the Rashtriya Gram SwarajAbhiyan (RGSA), a total of 2,75,893 participants have been trained through the Specialised Module on Own Source Revenue (OSR).
(ii) In 2025, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj launched the Atma Nirbhar Panchayat Special Award (ANPSA) to promote Atmanirbharta through the augmentation of Own Source Revenue (OSR) by Panchayats.
(iii) The Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) has also developed the SAMARTH Panchayat portal, a dedicated digital platform that facilitates the generation of tax & non-tax demands and collection thereof, maintenance of tax registers, and online tracking of revenue.
(iv)
With a view to support States and Union Territories in strengthening their legal and institutional framework for Own Source Revenue, the Ministry has formulated the Model Own Source Revenue Rules as a guiding framework for consideration by the States/Union Territories. These Model Rules are advisory in nature and are intended to serve as a reference for strengthening the Own Source Revenue framework of Panchayats. States and Union Territories may adopt, adapt or modify these Model Rules, either in full or in part, as considered appropriate, keeping in view their existing legal provisions, administrative arrangements and local requirements.
(v)
The implementation of the SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages Abadi and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas) Scheme, launched in April, 2020, lays a robust foundation for the growth of property taxes in rural areas, ultimately leading to enhanced OSR generation and improved financial self‑sufficiency for RLBs.
With the objective to improve oversight and monitoring and to ensure transparency and accountability in the disbursal and utilisation of Central Finance Commission grants by Panchayati Raj Institutions in the States, including Chhattisgarh, the Ministry has launched the eGramSwaraj web portal (https://egramswaraj.gov.in) since April 2020, which integrates all financial functions of Panchayats-from planning to payment. The progress data obtained from this system is displayed on the portal, available in the public domain, for concurrent monitoring at the State, District, and Block levels.
The eGramSwaraj is integrated with the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) for the Panchayats (GPs), facilitating real-time digital payments to vendors and service providers. Additionally, the AuditOnline application was launched in April 2020 to enable online auditing of Panchayat accounts and their financial management. This tool facilitates the transparent utilisation of Central Finance Commission funds and enhances Panchayat-level financial oversight.
This information was given by Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha on 12th August 2026.

title: ATMANIRBHAR PANCHAYAT PROGRAM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme is a four‑year initiative aimed at making Panchayats financially self‑sufficient by generating Own Source Revenue (OSR) through projects that utilize unexplored local assets. Proposals are selected through a State and National level open challenge system, with 50 projects taken up in the first year and 100 each in the following three years. The programme provides technical assistance ensuring participatory planning through mandatory Gram Sabha clearance. Only elected Gram and Block Panchayats with at least three years of tenure and minimum OSR thresholds (₹50 lakh for Gram Panchayats and ₹1 crore for Block Panchayats, with relaxed norms for Northeast and Hill States) are eligible. Panchayats are facilitated through technical assistance in refining the initial ideas into detailed, sustainable, bankable project concepts, in the preparation of project-related documents, in exploring funding options such as Public-Private Partnership (PPP), CSR funding, and convergence of schemes. They are also assisted in preparing Request for Proposal (RFP), including Model Contract documents / Agreements for issuance by the appropriate authority as per the procurement rules of the State concerned and in achieving financial closure. The entire process of submission and selection is managed through a dedicated digital portal, reinforcing transparency and efficiency. As on 04.08.2026, a total of 30 project proposals from 28 Panchayats have been received at Centre level on the designated portal.
As per the Programme Guidelines, States may associate financial institutions like NABARD, HUDCO, etc. in the State-level evaluation committees to provide technical and financial advice on Panchayat proposals.
The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme is expected to enhance Panchayats’ Own Source Revenue (OSR) in direct alignment with the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s recommendations by moving them away from grant dependency and towards sustainable revenue generation. The Sixteenth Finance Commission has emphasized that performance grants to Rural Local Bodies should be linked to measurable increases in OSR, and this initiative provides Panchayats with the structured support to achieve that. Through a national challenge process, Panchayats are encouraged to develop bankable projects using local assets, with technical assistance provided instead of direct financial aid. Financing is facilitated through PPP, CSR, convergence of schemes, and institutional credit, ensuring projects are viable and revenue-generating. Mandatory Gram Sabha approval and digital monitoring guarantee transparency and accountability, while financial institutions and technical team lend financial and infrastructure expertise. In this way, Panchayats are empowered to consistently raise their own revenues, qualify for performance-linked grants, and progressively become financially self-reliant institutions as envisaged by the Sixteenth Finance Commission.
This information was given by Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha on 12th August 2026.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF RASHTRIYA GRAM SWARAJ ABHIYAN (RGSA) IN WEST BENGAL
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:35PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject and part of the State list of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/ UTs. The main objective of the scheme is to strengthen the capacity of Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by imparting training to Elected Representatives (ERs), Panchayat Functionaries and other stakeholders to develop their governance capabilities for leadership roles, enabling the Gram Panchayats and Local bodies to function effectively across all States/UTs including the State of West Bengal.
Apart from different trainings, the Scheme also supports development of Panchayat infrastructure like Gram Panchayat Bhawan, Computer and Co-location (on a limited scale) of Common Service Centers (CSCs) in Gram Panchayat Bhawan to the States/ UTs including in the State of West Bengal.
Under Revamped RGSA, the Central Empowered Committee of RGSA accords approval to the units under various components based on the Annual Action Plan (AAP) submitted by the State/UT. During the last four years (FY 2022-23 to FY 2025-26), an amount of Rs.130.65 crore was released as Central Share to the State of West Bengal under the Scheme. Out of which, Rs.268.26 crore has been utilized by the State. Utilization of funds includes Central Share, State Share and unspent balance from previous years.
A total of 5,17,632 elected representatives of the State of West Bengal were trained on various aspects on rural governance from FY 2022-23 to FY 2025-26. In addition, 199 units for the construction of Panchayat Bhawans and 1,712 units of Computers were approved under the scheme from FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26. The State has reported that 124 Panchayat Bhawan have been constructed and 1,185 units of computers have been procured during FY 2023-24 to 2026-27 (as on 5th August 2026).
The State has also reported that all stakeholders of Panchayati Raj Institutions are invited to participate in various training programmes conducted under the Scheme.
Revamped RGSA is demand-driven in nature. Funds are released to States/UTs based on the Annual Action Plans approved by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC), the pace of expenditure by the State and submission of requisite document for release of funds. The funds are utilized only for the approved components as prioritized by the States/UTs. The Ministry releases the funds under the scheme to States/UTs only. Rs.8.00 crore as Central Share in the 1st Instalment was released to the State of West Bengal in the FY 2026-27 (as on 10th July 2026).
As informed by the State, 199 units of the construction of Gram Panchayat Bhawans have been approved from FY 2023-24 to 2025-26 under the scheme of Revamped RGSA, out of which 124 units have been completed till 5th August 2026 and remaining 75 units are different stages of completion. As per the information submitted in the Annual Action Plan of RGSA in the FY 2025-26 by the State, only 87 Gram Panchayats out of 3,339 do not have own building. Under Revamped RGSA Scheme, component wise fund has not been released to the States/UTs. State/UTs utilized the funds based on the approved components of their AAPs as per the priority.
To promote e-enablement of Panchayats, the Ministry is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP), which has strengthened transparency, efficiency and governance at the grassroots level. As per the information available on Government e Marketplace (GeM) Portal, 267 Panchayats have adopted/ on-boarded on GeM. 1,881 Gram Panchayats have uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development Plan on eGramSwaraj Portal for the Plan Year 2026-27 in the State of West Bengal as on 06.08.2026. As informed by the State Govt. of West Bengal, a total of 10,111 elected representatives have been trained as on date under the scheme in FY 2026-27.
This information was given by Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha on 12th August 2026.

title: STRENGTHENING DIGITAL PANCHAYAT GOVERNANCE THROUGH EGRAMSWARAJ
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) with the objective of strengthening transparency, efficiency, and accountability in the functioning of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) through digital enablement across all States. The eGramSwaraj application has been integrated with various digital governance platforms to enhance planning, financial management and service delivery in Panchayati Raj Institutions. The major integrations are as follows:
Public Financial Management System (PFMS):
For online fund management, accounting and end-to-end digital payments to vendors and beneficiaries.
Government e-Marketplace (GeM):
To facilitate procurement of goods and services by Panchayati Raj Institutions in a transparent and efficient manner.
BSNL:
To enable panchayat to apply for new internet connection and bill payment of BharatNet connection through eGramSwaraj.
BHASHINI:
To provide multilingual and AI-enabled language translation and voice-based services for improved accessibility of the platform.
India Meteorological Department (IMD):
To provide weather-related information for supporting local planning and decision-making by Panchayati Raj Institutions.
These integrations have been made available through the eGramSwaraj platform for all States and expected to benefit all
Gram Panchayats across the country using the eGramSwaraj platform.
Further, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj launched
SabhaSaar
, an AI-enabled voice-to-text meeting summarisation tool, that enables structured capture and summarisation of Gram Sabha proceedings and supports monitoring of key parameters such as frequency and type of Gram Sabha meetings and participation. The platform captures agenda-wise discussions, decisions, and participation details, and the generated minutes are made available to Panchayat functionaries for review, validation and final acceptance. SabhaSaar has been made available to all States/UTs.
During the FY 2025–26, out of a total of 2,58,725 Gram Panchayats and equivalent across the States, 2,55,251 (98.65%) of them have uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) on e-Gram Swaraj and 2,45,839 Gram Panchayats and equivalents (95%) have made payments amounting to ₹57,337 crore through the e-GramSwaraj–PFMS interface. Further a total of 1,35,956 Gram Panchayats and equivalent have used the SabhaSaar tool for automated meeting summarization and over 3,57,020 minutes of the meeting have been processed across States/UTs.
These initiatives are expected to enhance transparency through digital workflows and real-time monitoring, improve accountability by ensuring standardized planning and financial management processes, facilitate evidence-based decision-making through dashboards and reports, reduce manual intervention, and promote ease of governance by providing an integrated digital platform for planning, accounting, monitoring, and implementation of Panchayat activities.
This information was given by Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha on 12th August 2026.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: MISSION KARMAYOGI
ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Mission Karmayogi, the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) was approved by the Government of India in September 2020 with an aim of transitioning from a 'rule- based' to 'role-based' HR system and creating civil servants with a global outlook while being rooted in Indian ethos.
The iGOT Karmayogi digital learning portal, established under the Mission Karmayogi, has continued to expand rapidly in scale and reach. The portal, currently, has more than 1.7 crore registered users. It hosts more than 5,600 courses across domain, functional, and behavioural competencies, covering a total of 6,953 hours of learning. Courses are available in 23 languages, including English and Hindi, enabling wide accessibility and alignment with regional and linguistic needs. There have been more than 14.42 crore course completions on iGOT so far.
To strengthen continuous capacity building and digital learning across all levels of government, employees from Central Government, States/UTs, as well as urban and rural local bodies have been onboarded on iGOT. To ensure role-based training, Capacity Building Plans are being made for all Ministries, Departments, and Organisations (MDOs). The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), along with the Capacity Building Commission (CBC) and SPV Karmayogi Bharat (KB) continuously monitors the progress and provides necessary support to all stakeholders in this regard. Government employees are also nudged and encouraged towards digital learning, and spirit of continuous learning is promoted through special initiatives like the National Learning Week - Karmayogi Saptah (held in October 2024) and the SADHANA Saptah (April 2026).
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

The Government has undertaken several measures to strengthen the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS). Major reforms include adoption of next-generation technologies to enhance system capabilities, introduction of the Grievance Redressal Assessment and Index (GRAI) to benchmark the performance of Ministries and Departments, publication of monthly CPGRAMS reports for transparency and monitoring, capacity building of grievance officers through Sevottam, integration with the grievance portals of Central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs, multilingual grievance registration and translation facility through integration with Bhashini, operationalization of the Feedback Call Centre, availability of CPGRAMS through the mobile application and Common Service Centres (CSCs), reduction of prescribed grievance disposal timeline from 30 days to 21 days, and launch of 'Samadhan Didi', an AI-powered multilingual voice-first chatbot for grievance registration.
Further, to improve the quality of grievance redressal, the Comprehensive Guidelines on Handling of Public Grievances, issued in August 2024, mandates establishment of dedicated Grievance Cells in Ministries/Departments, appointment of experienced nodal officers, monitoring of pendency and citizen feedback, emphasis on root cause analysis, and strengthened escalation mechanisms. In addition, a dedicated Review Meeting Module has been operationalised in CPGRAMS to facilitate senior-level review of public grievances to further improve the efficiency and quality of grievance redressal.

title: Safety Fencing Along 19,700 km of Railway Tracks to Prevent Trespassing and Ensure Safe Train Operations
subtitle:
Indian Railways Takes Legal Action Against Offenders of Stone Pelting Under Relevant Provisions of Law to Provide Safety to Passengers and Protect Railway Property

Awareness Programmes Including OPERATION SATHI to Sensitize People and Regular Coordination with GRP/Local Police to Curb Stone Pelting Incidents on Trains
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Legal action is taken against the offenders of stone pelting under the relevant provision of law. The following preventive measures are taken by the Railways to safeguard the lives of passengers and damage to Railway Property:
Regular drives are conducted against anti-social elements like drunkard, mischievous elements etc. in the effected section/black spots and the apprehended persons are prosecuted under legal provisions of law.
The train escorting parties have been sensitized to remain more vigilant in the vulnerable sections/spots, where incidents of vandalizing on trains are frequently reported.
Various awareness programme including OPERATION SATHI are conducted regularly in inhabited areas adjacent to Railway track to sensitize people towards the menace of stone pelting and its consequences.
Detailed guidelines have been issued regarding action to be taken to control incidents of stone pelting on moving trains. Analysis of these incidents followed by substantive action is taken to curb these incidents.
Regular co-ordination with GRP/Local Police is maintained by RPF, sharing the critical information to control the menace of pelting of stones on trains.
State Level Security Committee of Railways (SLSCR) have been constituted for all State Union Territories under the Chairmanship of respective Director General of Police Commissioner of States/Union Territories for regular monitoring and review of security arrangements of the Railways.
Safety of train operations is accorded top priority on Indian Railways (IR). Pedestrian subways are also being provided with safety fencing in order to facilitate crossing of railway alignment by cattle, pedestrians and smaller vehicles.
Till date, about 19,700 km of fencing has been provided along the railway tracks in Indian Railways which includes sections situated in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
This information was provided by the Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, in a reply to a question in the Lok Sabha today.

With a view to expand digital mode of procurement of reserved as well as unreserved tickets Railways has launched RailOne App on 01.07.2025. This App enables passengers to book reserved as well as unreserved tickets on mobile phone. This App combines all the public facing services of Indian Railways like reserved ticketing, unreserved ticketing and platform ticketing, train enquiry, PNR enquiry, Railmadad, etc. into a single platform. This, in effect, brings the Passenger reservation system facility to passenger's palm.  The App facilitates users to access multiple services through Single-Sign-On (SSO) facility eliminating the necessity of downloading multiple Applications of Railways & remembering several passwords.

The National Train Enquiry System (NTES), implemented in the year 2000, provides passengers with near real-time train running information, including arrival/departure status and train schedules through multiple interfaces such as enquiry counters, the NTES website, mobile applications (Android & iOS) and the nationwide Rail Enquiry Number 139. Its key features include Spot Your Train, Live Station, Train Schedule, and Trains between Stations, enabling passengers to access authentic and reliable information conveniently. The NTES mobile application, launched in October 2014 (Android) and October 2015 (iOS), has recorded more than 4.5 crore downloads on Android and 16 lakh downloads on iOS as on 01.08.2026. At present, NTES handles about 80,000 concurrent users and processes over 6 crore enquiries daily. It has been generally appreciated by the passengers.
The deployment of the National Train Enquiry System (NTES), which provides passengers with easy access to authentic and near real-time train running information through multiple digital platforms including the website, mobile applications and Rail Enquiry Number 139, has significantly reduced the need for passengers to visit railway enquiry counters. Consequently, this has helped in reducing queues and waiting time at enquiry counters.
In cases of train cancellation, the online e-ticketing system NGeT(Next Generation E-ticketing) automatically initiates the process of refund immediately after the scheduled time of departure of the train and the applicable refund is credited to the passenger's bank account. Automatic refunds linked to train cancellation are presently available only for e-Tickets booked online and are not available for counter tickets in which case the passenger holding counter ticket is required to visit nearest PRS counter.
RailOne is the Official App of Indian Railways which provides integrated platform for all public facing services of IR. It offers reserved, unreserved and platform ticketing, journey plan, train information, passenger support and allied railway services through a single, seamless mobile application.
Presently approximately 89% of the reserved tickets are booked online as compared to about 49% in 2013-14. Unreserved tickets booked through various non-counter modes has increased to nearly 39%.

title: Indian Railways Approves Provision of Kavach Version 4.0 on 660 Route Km of Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway at ₹295 crore
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Indian Railways has approved the provision of Kavach Version 4.0 on 660 Route Km of the Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway (NER) at an estimated cost of ₹295 crore.
The work has been approved under the umbrella work “Provision of Kavach with communication backbone of Long-Term Evolution (LTE) on balance sections of Indian Railways.”
Kavach is India's indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system designed to prevent Signal Passed at Danger (SPAD) incidents and train collisions through continuous monitoring of train movements. The system automatically applies brakes whenever required, enables trains to safely operate at maximum permissible speeds, improves operational reliability and supports safe train operations even during adverse weather conditions such as dense fog.
The approved work covers the balance sections of the Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway. The provision of Kavach Version 4.0 will further strengthen the safety infrastructure on the identified railway sections.

title: Indian Railways Approves Construction of 4 Lane ROB at Geratpur-Ahmedabad Section in Gujarat at ₹153 Crore
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a major step towards safer and smoother movement of road traffic in Gujarat, Indian Railways has approved the construction of a 4 lane Road Over Bridge at Level Crossing No. 305 on the Geratpur-Ahmedabad section of Western Railway. The work has been sanctioned at a cost of ₹153 crore.
The project has been sanctioned under Western Railway's ongoing umbrella work for construction of road over and under bridges, foot over bridges, drainage improvement and rebuilding of road over and under bridges.
The crossing lies in a densely populated urban area, which calls for longer approaches and a larger structure. The railway bridge portion will have a total length of 106 metres. It will comprise two composite girders of 53 metres each. A viaduct of 150 metres will follow. The railway approach will extend to 595 metres.
Safer and Faster Movement for Commuters
The new Road Over Bridge will remove the need for road users to wait at the level crossing. It will allow uninterrupted movement of vehicles across the railway line at all hours. Road users in the area will gain safer passage, shorter travel time and relief from congestion at the crossing.
The approval reflects Indian Railways' continued commitment towards elimination of level crossings, improved public safety and creation of modern and efficient transport infrastructure across the country.

date:

content:
Government in Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is primarily responsible for development and maintenance of National Highways (NHs). The Government has inter-alia decided to focus on development of Access controlled National High Speed Corridors (HSCs) / Expressways, development of ring road / bypasses of cities with population of more than One Lakh with priority on those cities which have population of more than Five Lakh, development of coastal roads, connectivity of ports as per the prioritization of Ministry of Shipping, Ports and Waterways, connectivity of airports as per the prioritization of Ministry of Civil Aviation and connectivity to Industrial nodes as per the priority of National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) for improving the logistics efficiency of the country. These steps are directed towards broadening investment opportunities in highway infrastructure.
To attract more private players and make investment opportunities more attractive, the Government has taken several initiatives like reforms in Model Concession Agreement for Public Private Partnership (PPP) Projects, reforms in model contracts for monetization of NHs through Toll Operate and Transfer (TOT) basis, introduction of Public InvIT to widen investment scope, Stakeholder Conferences held with concessionaires, financiers, and major government bodies to showcase investment opportunities to private players as well as understand & address investors' concerns etc.
Major amendments in the standard bidding and concession documents for Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) projects on NHs include: -
Enhanced bidder eligibility by permitting participation of Fund Houses on their financial strength. Upon successful award of project, they shall engage EPC contractors possessing the requisite technical experience for execution of the works.
Learning from past litigations and contractual interpretations and for greater contractual clarity; provisions relating to Change in Ownership, Target Traffic, Damages, Compensation for Breach of Agreement, Compensation for Force Majeure Costs, Payment of Construction Support during the Construction Period in Capacity Augmentation projects, Compensation for Annual Passes, and Change of Scope have been amended.
Provision for payment of Termination Compensation before the Commercial Operation Date (COD) where the physical progress of the project is 20% or more, thereby protecting the interests of both the Concessionaire and the lenders.
Streamlined provisions relating to the determination of Debt Due to remove ambiguities and provide greater certainty in their application.
Streamlined Dispute Resolution mechanism – Dispute Resolution Board abolished; Disputes less than ₹ 10 Cr to be resolved through Arbitration and Disputes of ₹ 10 Cr and above through Conciliation or Mediation.
This information was given by Union Minister of Road Transport & Highways, Shri Nitin Gadkari in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

title: IMPLEMENTATION STATUS OF PM RAHAT SCHEME
date:

content:
In accordance with the legal mandate under Section 162 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the PM-RAHAT (Road Accident Victims' Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment) scheme was launched for nationwide implementation on 13.02.2026, with the primary objective of reducing fatalities due to road accidents by ensuring timely and uninterrupted medical care to road accident victims including during the critical Golden Hour i.e., the time period lasting one hour following a traumatic injury during which there is highest likelihood of preventing death by providing prompt medical care. The scheme provides treatment cover upto Rs. 1.5 lakh per victim, subject to a maximum cap of 7 days from the date of accident on any category of road. Further, the treatment cover will be available to all those victims who are involved in road accidents caused by use of motor vehicles.
As on 31.07.2026 since the launch of the scheme for nation-wide implementation on 13.02.2026, a total of 22,481 victims have benefitted from the scheme across 34 States/UTs. The State/UT-wise details are attached as
Annexure-I.
Against the total amount of the claims raised by the hospitals, State Health Agencies (SHA) have approved claims amounting to Rs.12.59 Crores. Out of which, Rs.10.56 Crores have been paid to the hospitals.
As per the Scheme guidelines notified vide S.O. 2489 (E) dated 04th June, 2025, designated hospitals under the Scheme, including empanelled hospitals under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) that comply with the guidelines issued by the National Health Authority (NHA) for this scheme shall be deemed designated hospitals for the purposes of the Scheme.
Further, States & UTs are advised to designate and onboard additional hospitals based on detailed guidelines dated 20.5.2025 issued by NHA.
Denial of admission or treatment under the Scheme amounts to non-compliance with the applicable Scheme provisions. States/UTs are empowered to take action under laws regulating clinical establishments, including the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, or the corresponding State-specific laws. Further, the hospital empanelment guidelines provide for disciplinary proceedings, suspension and de-empanelment in cases of non-compliance.
To ensure that victim reaches the hospital within Golden Hour, convergence with the 112 Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) has been established, so that a victim or Good Samaritan may dial 112 and obtain details of the nearest designated hospital and also seek ambulance support.

title: Over 50,000 Saplings Planted Across 31 States on Hariyali Amavasya Under Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s Green Initiative
subtitle:
Vriksh Mitra Parivar Drives Nationwide Plantation Campaign Under PM Modi’s ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ Call

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Leads Major Tree Plantation Drive in Delhi on Hariyali Amavasya

Vriksh Mitra Parivar Emerges as the Face of a Nationwide Green Movement

Planting Trees Means Securing the Future: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Respect for Nature Is the Best Way to Protect Future Generations; The Real Commitment Is to Save Trees, Not Just Plant Them: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Delhi Has Learnt Much from Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s Green Initiative, Says Minister Shri Manjinder Singh Sirsa

Development Must Go Hand in Hand with Environmental Protection, Says Minister Shri Parvesh Verma
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
More than 50,000 saplings were planted across 31 states on the occasion of Hariyali Amavasya as part of a nationwide plantation drive led by Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan in collaboration with the “Vriksh Mitra Parivar.” The campaign drew further momentum from Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative. The program was held at the PBG Ground, Central Ridge, near Talkatora Stadium in New Delhi, where ministers, Members of Parliament, government officials, farmers, youth and citizens participated in the plantation drive. The program began with the watering of saplings and the singing of Vande Mataram, followed by mass plantation. Similar plantation drives were organised across villages, towns, panchayats and institutions in different parts of the country. Members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar played a key role in mobilising citizens and encouraging them to plant at least one tree.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Chouhan said Hariyali Amavasya is not only a religious occasion but also an opportunity to express gratitude towards nature. He said Indian traditions view human beings, animals, birds, rivers, mountains and trees as interconnected elements of the natural ecosystem. “Planting a tree is not just about adding greenery; it is an investment in the future of coming generations,” Shri Chouhan said, stressing that planting saplings must be accompanied by a commitment to their protection and regular care. The Union Minister urged every citizen to plant at least one tree each year and encourage five others to join the campaign. He suggested observing birthdays, wedding anniversaries, the birth of children and the death anniversaries of parents as “Vriksh Parv” by planting trees.
Shri Chouhan also called upon panchayats, urban local bodies and institutions to identify designated areas for plantation so that saplings can be protected and maintained over the long term. Highlighting the close link between environmental sustainability and agriculture, Shri Chouhan said environmental degradation directly affects farming, water availability, soil health and human well-being. He said that for farmers, access to water and maintaining soil health are as important as the availability of seeds and fertilisers. He called for greater adoption of Mission LiFE, energy conservation and reduced dependence on plastic to strengthen environmental protection. “Nature must not be exploited; its resources must be used responsibly and conserved for the future,” he said.
Delhi government's Cabinet Minister Shri Manjinder Singh Sirsa said the Delhi Government had drawn valuable lessons from Shri Chouhan’s initiative. He said more than one lakh people in Delhi have been connected with the campaign, while schools, colleges and other institutions are also being encouraged to participate in plantation activities. Shri Sirsa said citizens are increasingly coming forward to take a collective pledge for environmental protection and contribute to the plantation drive.
Delhi government's Cabinet Minister Shri Parvesh Verma said the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative should inspire every citizen to take responsibility for protecting the environment. He said development and environmental conservation must go hand in hand, adding that sustainable development requires a balance between infrastructure expansion and preservation of green cover.
The program was attended by Member of Parliament Shri Darshan Singh Choudhary, representatives of various institutions, officials from agricultural universities, personnel from ICAR, DARE and KVKs, and a large number of members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar. The nationwide drive was positioned as a tree plantation exercise as well as an effort to build sustained public participation in environmental conservation. The campaign emphasised that planting a sapling is only the first step, while ensuring its survival and growth is an equally important responsibility. Members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar are continuing to take this message to communities across the country.

title: AI uncovers hidden cancer stem cells responsible for tumour recurrence paving way to precision medicine
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 3:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A new artificial intelligence (AI) framework that identifies three distinct developmental states of cancer stem-like cells can help identify hidden cancer stem cells from thousands of patient samples and bring precision medicine one step closer to reality specially in areas with limited health facilities.
Cancer remains one of humanity's greatest medical challenges. Although modern treatments can destroy millions of cancer cells, a small population of cells often survives, allowing tumours to return, spread to distant organs and develop resistance to therapy.
Scientists have long believed that these rare cancer stem-like cells that help tumours survive and return and
are responsible for tumour recurrence, metastasis and treatment failure. However, because these cells are extremely rare and constantly change their identity, accurately detecting them has remained one of the biggest challenges in cancer research.
Researchers from S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences (SNBNCBS), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, in collaboration with Ashoka University, have now developed an artificial intelligence (AI) framework that reveals hidden cancer stem-like cell states from tumour gene-expression data.
This work led by Dr. Shubhasis Haldar builds upon the team's earlier AI platform, OncoMark, which accurately decoded the biological hallmarks that drive cancer progression across millions of cells with over 99% predictive accuracy.
By enabling researchers to measure the fundamental processes that fuel tumour growth, metastasis and drug resistance, OncoMark demonstrated how artificial intelligence can uncover complex biological information hidden within massive genomic datasets. Building on that success, the team has now turned its attention to one of cancer biology's most difficult problems—identifying the elusive stem-like cells that drive tumour evolution.
Their new framework, called ACSCeND (AI-based Cancer Stem-like Cell Profiler and Neoplasm Deconvoluter), goes beyond conventional methods that assign tumours a single "stemness" score. Instead, it identifies three distinct developmental states of cancer stem-like cells—pluripotent-like, multipotent-like and unipotent-like—providing an unprecedented view of tumour heterogeneity. The system combines knowledge learned from high-resolution single-cell sequencing with deep learning to analyse conventional bulk tumour RNA sequencing, allowing these hidden cell populations to be studied in thousands of patient samples where single-cell experiments are unavailable.
The researchers rigorously validated ACSCeND against existing computational approaches and showed that it consistently outperformed current methods across independent datasets and sequencing platforms. They then applied the framework to analyse more than 25,000 tumour samples from major international cancer databases, including TCGA and PRECOG. The analyses revealed that tumours enriched with highly potent, pluripotent-like cancer stem cells were associated with poorer patient survival, a greater likelihood of tumour recurrence and reduced response to modern immunotherapies.
Beyond identifying these dangerous cells, ACSCeND also uncovered the molecular programs that enable them to survive, adapt and evade the immune system. Such insights could help scientists discover new drug targets, identify patients who are more likely to relapse and design more effective precision cancer therapies.
Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming an indispensable partner in modern biomedical research. AI enables researchers to detect hidden biological patterns across enormous genomic datasets that would be impossible to analyse manually.
Studies such as OncoMark and ACSCeND illustrate how AI can accelerate discoveries that ultimately improve cancer diagnosis, predict treatment response and guide the development of more effective therapies.
